Deze leden vragen wat er gebeurt als de sanering niet het gewenste resultaat met zich meebrengt?
Requests concrete case studies and cost reconciliation with the budget to make the effects of the noise-law changes transparent to Parliament.
They therefore request the government to send several case studies on rail and road to the House and answer at least the following questions in them
Zij verzoeken de regering daarom om enkele casussen rond spoor en weg aan de Kamer te doen toekomen en daarin in elk geval antwoord te geven op de volgende vragen
Asks how municipalities were involved, whether exposure targets are achievable within budget, and whether annual reporting to Parliament on exceedance decisions and exemptions is anchored in law.

Objects that key political choices are left to ministerial regulation and AMvB without prior parliamentary discussion, and asks for a pre-consultation procedure and AMvB-level basic rules for measurement methods and traffic forecasts.

These members note that the mentioned AMvBs contain some political choices, such as the formulation of the efficiency criterion, and find that these choices cannot be made before the House, if it wishes, has been able to discuss them.

Deze leden constateren dat genoemde AMvB's enkele politieke keuzes bevatten, zoals de formulering van het doelmatigheidscriterium, en vinden dat deze keuzes niet kunnen worden gemaakt voordat de Kamer, als zij dit wenst, erover heeft kunnen spreken.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that the noise production ceiling bill for Rijkswegen and hoofdspoorwegen insufficiently ensures legal certainty for citizens, criticising joint ministerial decision-making, delegation of material norms to ministerial regulation, the 1.5 dB generic headroom for existing infrastructure and the supervision arrangements. The government's nader rapport adopts several points (e.g. reallocating powers, moving the road-map and financial efficiency criteria into the AMvB, adding a new article on the Afdeling 3.4 Awb exception and a saneringsplan), but maintains the generic 1.5 dB headroom and the joint competence for the overschrijdingsbesluit, with reasoning for each.
concerns: Joint decision-making by the ministers of VROM and VenW is insufficiently motivated given VenW's role as road manager, so competences were reallocated to one minister where possible.

Material norms such as best available techniques and the financial efficiency criterion should be set in the law or AMvB rather than ministerial regulation; the government followed this for some provisions but not for the concept of best available techniques.

Procedural guarantees including the exclusion of Afdeling 3.4 Awb and the circle of interested parties should be laid down in the law; the government moved the circle into the law but limited the exception rather than removing it entirely.

The generic 1.5 dB headroom for existing infrastructure is too far-reaching for citizens' protection, including situations exceeding maximum values and earlier higher-value decisions; the government kept the generic headroom while adding a saneringsbepaling and budget.
Supervision arrangements should be described and VenW should not play a role in enforcement; the memorie van toelichting was expanded on preventive supervision by the Inspectie.
Several redactional comments on the bill's text were adopted.

32261.s: The bill amends the Wet op de beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) to let the minister give effect to foreign-imposed restrictions on practice for registrants, and adds a new article 36a allowing, by general administrative order, a five-year experiment in which designated health professionals may independently indicate and perform reserved acts. It also allows subdelegation of certain registration and detail rules to ministerial regulation.
32261.j: The memorandum justifies the new experimental power as necessary because the current act-by-decree route under art. 37 requires a bill within six months, which is unsuitable for emerging task-shifting professions that need time to develop evidence.
q: With this amendment the aim is to responsibly keep pace with new developments and give new professions a better chance to develop.
Met de wijziging wordt beoogd op verantwoorde wijze aan te sluiten bij nieuwe ontwikkelingen en nieuwe beroepen hiermee beter de kans te bieden zich te ontwikkelen.
d: registration fees and rules, now also by ministerial regulation
designating medicines and equipment for midwives
designating medicines and equipment for other professionals
five-year experiment allowing designated professionals to perform reserved acts independently, deviating from art. 36 and the Geneesmiddelenwet
granting a protected professional title during the experiment
p: Registration must be refused or struck off automatically on foreign restrictions, with the minister empowered to disapply this in cases of overriding unfairness.

Reserved medical acts can be transferred to new professional categories by general administrative order, without the usual statutory amendment, for up to five years with an evaluation and a four-week voorhang period.
Prescriptions by experiment-designated professionals are treated as valid prescriptions and disciplinary law applies to them, with reduced sanctions since they are not registered.

parties: Questions the five-year experimental status, the content of the AMvB, and the evaluation criteria, and asks how the experiment and its oversight are organised.
The Council of State is critical of this form.
De Raad van State is kritisch over deze vorm.
Asks whether quality is safeguarded during the experiment, whether monitoring should be interim, and whether disciplinary law should apply uniformly to new professions.
These members ask whether quality is sufficiently safeguarded during the experiment and why the government does not choose interim monitoring.
Deze leden vragen of de kwaliteit hiermee gedurende het experiment wel voldoende geborgd is, en vragen waarom de regering niet kiest voor tussentijds monitoren.
Worries about further liberalisation, unclear new professions, the scope of delegated reserved acts, and the Chamber's ability to exercise control over AMvB and ministerial regulations.
Since 1993 this means a further liberalisation of the Wet BIG with the risks that entails.
Na 1993 betekent dit een verdere liberalisering van de Wet BIG met de risico’s van dien.
Broadly supports task reallocation but asks for normative safeguards for future professions and clarity on disciplinary law and the relation to the AWBZ.
On that point these members can agree with the government's position.
Op dat punt kunnen deze leden zich dus vinden in de positie van de regering.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill amending the BIG Act to allow temporary task reallocation via AMvB, cross-border measures recognition, and broader subdelegation. The Raad raised major objections to the experimental clause (unbounded scope, missing guarantees, reversibility) and to automatic recognition of foreign sanctions, and the government's reply accepted several points (hardship clause, subdelegation narrowed, scope limited) while rejecting others (registration and title, parliamentary procedure).
concerns: The Raad objected that the experimental clause lacks guarantees on registration and title protection, creating legal uncertainty, and the government narrowed the clause and added an educational title option but kept registration excluded.
The Raad objected that the experimental power is unbounded in scope and the government limited the eligible categories to those with approved training.
The Raad advised a hardship clause for automatic recognition of foreign sanctions, which the government adopted.
The Raad objected to the broad subdelegation to ministerial regulation, and the government narrowed the provisions.
The Raad advised removing or motivating the procedure requiring parliamentary involvement before the AMvB, which the government did not fully accept.
The Raad distinguished EU/EEA from third-country sanctions and advised separate scrutiny, which the government addressed through the hardship clause.

32270.s: The bill allows bachelor graduates who complete an educational minor of at least 30 study points to be appointed as teachers in lower secondary and the first three years of upper secondary education (mavo and the first three years of havo/vwo), limited to subjects closely related to their degree. It amends the Wet op het voortgezet onderwijs by adding paragraph 1a and 1b to article 33, and adds a paragraph to article 7.6 of the Wet op het hoger onderwijs en wetenschappelijk onderzoek requiring universities to enable students to meet the competence requirements.
32270.j: The memorandum justifies the new route by the expected shortage of academically qualified teachers as experienced teachers retire, and the ministerial regulation is justified as a technical list of related subjects drawn up with VO-raad and VSNU.
q: On the basis of this proposal, a relatedness table will be established by ministerial regulation, to which the universities must adhere.
Op basis van dit voorstel wordt bij ministeriële regeling een verwantschapstabel vastgesteld, waar de universiteiten zich aan moeten houden
d: Artikel I (art. 33, lid 1b Wet op het voortgezet onderwijs)
list of bachelor programmes and subjects qualifying for the restricted teaching competence

parties: Welcomes the bill as a response to the teacher shortage and asks about the number of minors, progression to master's level and the content of the agreements between VO-raad and universities.
Already at the start of this cabinet period, the coalition made averting the threatened teacher shortage one of its policy priorities.
Al aan het begin van deze kabinetsperiode heeft de coalitie het afwenden van het dreigende lerarentekort tot één van haar speerpunten van haar beleid gemaakt.
Asks about the status of the qualification granted and whether subject-matter relevance of university programmes is strictly enforced, and how the teacher register standards relate to NVAO advice.
How will the competence requirements for subject teachers in the professional register relate to the positive NVAO advice on universities' proposals for educational minors, the members ask.

Hoe gaan de bekwaamheidseisen voor de vakdocenten in het beroepsregister zich verhouden tot de positieve advisering door het NVAO over de voorstellen van universiteiten inzake educatieve minoren, zo vragen de leden.
Sees the educational minor as lowering teaching quality, citing Raad van State warnings about lower entry requirements, and asks how the government responds.
The Council of State also sees risks to the quality of education if teachers are appointed who must meet lower requirements.
Ook de Raad van State ziet risico’s voor de kwaliteit van het onderwijs als leraren benoemd worden die aan minder hoge eisen hoeven te voldoen.
Supports the bill but asks whether graduates are sufficiently qualified, citing the Council of State's quality concern, and whether results of the existing minor are known.
The Council of State also points to the risks to education quality if teachers are appointed who need to meet lower requirements than currently.

Ook de Raad van State wijst in dit verband op de risico’s die kunnen ontstaan voor de kwaliteit van het onderwijs als leraren worden benoemd die aan minder hoge eisen hoeven te voldoen dan thans het geval is.
Supports the minor as a way to attract academics but worries it must not reduce quality or deter students from full first-degree training.
The quality of teachers must not suffer from the introduction of the educational minor.
De kwaliteit van de leraren mag niet leiden onder de invoering van de educatieve minor.
Asks whether students may be lured away from deeper subject study at master's level, possibly lowering knowledge levels.

The members ask whether there is not a risk that students will more readily forgo further deepening and subject-specific training, usually at master's level, when they are lured into teaching earlier.

De leden vragen of niet het gevaar bestaat dat studenten eerder af zullen zien van verdere verdieping en vakgerichte scholing, doorgaans in de master, wanneer zij eerder worden verleid om les te gaan geven.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill extending the ability to appoint bachelor graduates with an educational minor as teachers in lower secondary and the first three years of upper-level secondary education, accepting the goal but raising quality, sub-degree pathway, and progression concerns and recommending revisions. The government's reply addresses each point, stating teachers will meet the same competence requirements, that quality assurance applies, that the minor will not displace existing pathways, and that a new subsidy scheme is being prepared.
concerns: The Afdeling notes the bill is a partial answer to the teacher shortage and supports the policy aim of measures to address it.

The Afdeling says the explanatory memorandum lacks an assessment of how the scheme fits with maintaining teacher quality, and advises supplementing it with proof that quality and pedagogical-didactic preparation are guaranteed; the government revised the memorandum and argues quality is safeguarded by equivalent competence requirements and accreditation.

The Afdeling raises the risk that the three-year educational-minor route displaces the four-year second-degree and kopopleiding pathways and increases the risk for beginning teachers; the government denies displacement and cites an induction trajectory and CAO provisions.

The Afdeling flags that teachers pursuing a master's to gain upper-secondary competence will need to study alongside work or interrupt employment, and advises a new subsidy scheme since the existing lerarenbeurs window is too narrow; the government says a new scheme is being prepared and the memorandum was amended.

The Afdeling makes a redactional remark proposing deletion of wording in article 33(1a) of the WVO; the government did not adopt it, arguing the Afdeling overlooked that article 33(1)(b) under 1° and 2° applies and can be deviated from.

32315.s: The bill amends the Gemeentewet, Provinciewet and Waterschapswet so that municipal councils, provincial states and water board general boards may, within rules set by the ministers, take a broader view of a person's assets when granting full or partial remission of local taxes. It is a small expansion of local discretion over debt relief, with the rules themselves to be set by ministerial regulation.
32315.j: The memorandum justifies the broader discretion as giving local authorities room for social policy while keeping the character of the remission scheme, and cites the economic situation increasing demand for remission.
q: To give decentralised authorities room for social policy while not entirely abandoning the character of the remission scheme, the policy freedom of decentralised authorities to remit tax debts was broadened.

Om de decentrale overheden ruimte te geven voor sociaal beleid en toch niet helemaal het karakter van de kwijtscheldingsregeling los te laten, is per 1 januari 1995 de beleidsvrijheid van de decentrale overheden tot het kwijtschelden van belastingschulden verruimd
d: ARTIKEL I, ARTIKEL II, ARTIKEL III
rules on how assets are counted for remission of local taxes
p: ARTIKEL I, ARTIKEL II, ARTIKEL III
Local councils and boards gain discretion to assess assets more generously than the national collection regulation allows, within nationally set rules.

parties: Welcomes local tailoring of remission policy and entrepreneur eligibility, distinguishing this from local income policy; asks about the revenue effect of tariffs.
The CDA members appreciate that tailored arrangements can be made at the decentralised level.
Het spreekt de leden van de CDA-fractie aan dat er op decentraal niveau maatwerk kan worden geleverd.
Positive about broader discretion for local authorities but asks whether they should have more freedom for people with debts and whether the norm should reach 120% of the welfare norm.
Does the government agree with these members that local authorities should, beyond the asset test and cost of living, have more freedom regarding people with debts to remit local taxes?

Is de regering met deze leden van mening dat decentrale overheden, naast de vermogenstoets en kosten van bestaan, ook ten aanzien van mensen met schulden meer vrijheid moeten hebben om lokale belastingen kwijt te kunnen schelden?
Welcomes more options but questions the wide variation between municipalities and water boards, asks whether remission should be mandatory at 100% of the welfare norm, and raises hardship cases.
Is the government intending to oblige local authorities to grant remission to people with an income up to and including 100% of the welfare norm?
Is de regering voornemens om decentrale overheden te verplichten om kwijtschelding te verlenen aan mensen met een inkomen tot en met 100% van de bijstandsnorm?
Critical of the bill; asks for justification of the broader discretion, the financial consequences and whether other taxpayers will bear the cost.
They note that they are critical of this bill.
Zij merken op, dat zij kritisch tegenover dit wetsvoorstel staan.
Takes no position given the economic crisis and expected cuts; asks about the amounts remitted and their distribution.
Given the economic crisis and expected cuts, they will for now not take a position.
Zij zullen gezien de economische crisis en de verwachte bezuinigingen vooralsnog geen stand-punt innemen.
Endorses the starting point of the bill and has no questions.
They endorse the starting point of the bill.
Zij onderschrijven het uitgangspunt van het wetsvoorstel.

v.summary: The Raad van State supports the bill widening municipal, provincial and water board discretion to grant remission of taxes (vermogenstoets aligned with WWB and small self-employed eligible), but asks for changes; the government rejected the request to amend the Uitvoeringsregeling instead, followed the advice to drop the self-employed provision, kept the existing wording on 'besluiten' and adopted the drafting remarks.
concerns: The Raad asked whether the asset threshold should instead be changed by amending the Uitvoeringsregeling, which would be simpler and reduce conflicting rules; the government rejected this because the national and local tax rules serve different purposes.
The Raad saw no need for the provision extending remission to self-employed persons, since the Uitvoeringsregeling can handle this, and advised deleting it; the government followed this advice.

The Raad advised keeping the existing wording 'afwijkende regels stellen' rather than 'besluiten' to preserve the distinction between general rules and individual decisions; the government followed this.
The Raad gave a series of redactional remarks on the title, preamble, article numbering and wording, which the government adopted.

32360-IIA.s: This is the 2010 supplementary budget act (slotwet) for the Staten-Generaal (IIA) for fiscal year 2009, adjusting the budget appropriations and realised figures across parliamentary budget items. It sets the amounts in thousands of euros and makes the amendments effective from publication, with retroactive effect to 31 December of the budget year.
q: This is due to a deviation in faction costs and results from the factions' advance payment wishes.
Dit komt door een afwijking op de fractiekosten en is het gevolg van de bevoorschottingswensen van de fracties

32441.s: The bill amends the Dutch Port State Control Act to implement EU Directive 2009/16/EC, adding extended inspections, new grounds for refusing port access to repeatedly detained ships, and a complaints procedure. It delegates many technical inspection and procedural details to ministerial regulation, including rules on complaints handling.
32441.j: The explanatory memorandum justifies delegation mainly by the technical, detailed nature of the elements and their likely frequent amendment through EU comitology procedures.
q: Given the predominantly technical and detailed nature of these elements, and the fact that they may often be amended in parts within the comitology procedure, the technical aspects of the inspection procedure can be given content on the basis of article 5 of the Act.

Gelet op het overwegend technische en gedetailleerde karakter van deze elementen en het feit dat deze elementen naar verwachting op onderdelen in het kader van de comitologieprocedure veelvuldig kunnen worden gewijzigd, kan op grond van artikel 5 van de wet invulling worden gegeven aan de technische aspecten van de inspectieprocedure.
d: rules on inspection authorities implementing chapters II-V of the directive
Artikel I, onderdeel B (artikel 5, delegation basis extended)
technical aspects of the inspection procedure
port manager may, in agreement with the Minister, allow a refused ship to enter port for re-inspection
port manager, in agreement with the Minister, may admit a ship in cases of force majeure or overriding safety reasons
p: Allows the port manager, in agreement with the Minister, to admit ships otherwise refused entry in cases of force majeure or overriding safety reasons, with the captain required to take adequate safety measures.
Gives the Minister power to determine that an appeal against a refusal of port access does not suspend the decision, limiting suspensive effect of appeals against refusals.

parties: Welcomes risk-based, effective supervision and lower burdens, but asks the government to explain the scope of the new delegation basis in Article 5 and the reasons for it.
These members note that this delegation basis is described very summarily and ask the government to elaborate on the need for this additional delegation basis.
Deze leden constateren dat deze delegatiegrondslag zeer summier is omschreven en vragen of de regering nader in kan gaan op de noodzaak voor deze extra delegatiegrondslag.
Supports port state control and the new inspection regime as a way to tackle substandard shipping, and asks how long ships have to remedy deficiencies.
These members support the concept of port state control and consider it of great importance, because a number of flag states seriously fail in implementing and enforcing international standards.
Deze leden ondersteunen het concept van de havenstaatcontrole en vinden deze van groot belang, omdat een aantal vlaggenstaten ernstig in gebreke blijft.

Fully backs the amendment, sees risk-based inspections as avoiding unnecessary checks and favouring Dutch shipping companies, and supports extending the law to ships from the Netherlands Antilles and Aruba.
These members fully support this legislative amendment.
Deze leden staan volledig achter deze wetswijziging.

Asks for clarification of the claim that the new regime runs almost synchronously with the Paris MoU and how quickly other member states are implementing it, and whether consultation with the shipping sector took place.
These members ask what the government means by the phrasing that the new inspection regime runs 'almost synchronously' with the Paris MoU's New Inspection Regime.
De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen wat de regering bedoelt met de formulering dat het nieuwe inspectieregime «vrijwel synchroon» loopt met het «New Inspection Regime» van het ParisMoU.

Welcomes the risk profile but worries about reduced inspections, flexible application of the regime, shipping being refused entry, and costs shifting to the state; asks for the detailed risk profile to be submitted to parliament.
The SP members ask the government to submit to the House the detailed risk profile that will be used under the new inspection regime.
De leden van de SP-fractie vragen de regering om het gedetailleerde risicoprofiel waarmee onder het nieuwe inspectieregime gewerkt zal worden, aan de Kamer voor te leggen.

32450.s: The bill amends the General Administrative Law Act (Awb) and related statutes to streamline and modernise administrative procedure, including rules on replacement decisions during objection or appeal, passing over defects, hearing requirements, a 'grand chamber', independent conclusions by senior administrative judges, a relativity requirement, incidental appeals and a 'judicial loop'. It also consolidates administrative procedure rules into the Awb, reallocates jurisdiction among the Council of State, Central Appeals Tribunal and Trade and Industry Appeals Tribunal, and moves exemptions and fee rules into annexes.
32450.j: The memorandum justifies the changes as making administrative justice faster and more effective, achieving definitive resolution of disputes in one procedure while keeping legal protection intact.
q: In view of this, government policy aims to promote that as many disputes as possible are definitively settled after one administrative law procedure.
Gelet hierop is het kabinetsbeleid erop gericht te bevorderen dat zoveel mogelijk geschillen na afloop van één bestuursrechtelijke procedure definitief zijn beslecht.
d: allocation of jurisdiction among administrative judges
annual indexation of fees and amounts by ministerial regulation
p: Court may decide the case itself or order that the annulled decision's legal effects remain, shortening the administrative redo cycle.
Courts and bodies may let defective decisions stand where no claimant is harmed, and ignore rules that do not protect the claimant's interests, limiting annulment as a check on the executive.
Hearing may be skipped where the claimant does not respond within a set reasonable period.
Court may refer an appeal against a replacement decision to another body, shifting case handling away from the claimant's chosen forum.
Judicial loop: appeal against a decision implementing a higher court's ruling lies only with that higher court, bypassing the lower court.

parties: Asks whether the relativity requirement unduly limits challenges by those harmed by unlawful decisions and asks about the non-binding nature of conclusions for uniformity.
It could be argued that unlawfully taken decisions must always be challengeable by the person harmed.](Note: the relativity requirement would only limit this.)
Betoogd zou kunnen worden dat te allen tijde onrechtmatig genomen besluiten moeten kunnen worden aangevochten aanzien door de benadeelde.
Doubts that the large chamber and non-binding conclusions secure legal uniformity and questions the relativity requirement as the right solution.
The members believe the large chamber offers too little guarantee for safeguarding legal uniformity.
De aan het woord zijnde leden menen dat de grote kamer te weinig garantie biedt voor de bewaking van de rechtseenheid.
Argues the large chamber offers insufficient guarantees since referral is left to judges, and that non-binding conclusions will not secure uniformity.
Supports the reforms in principle but asks how citizens' interest in swift resolution is protected against the goal of legal uniformity, and what 'aannemelijk' means in the passing-of-defects rule.
These members do ask to what extent the citizen's legal protection is served by this.
Voornoemde leden hebben hierbij wel de vraag in hoeverre de rechtsbescherming van de burger hiermee gediend is.
Warns that limiting stakeholder rights and passing defects risk legal protection, questions the need for the relativity requirement, and will move to delete it by amendment.
For this reason they will submit an amendment to delete article 8:69a.
Om deze reden zullen zij een amendement indienen om artikel 8:69a te schrappen.
Asks why the general level of legal protection is lowered by the relativity requirement given it arises in few cases, and about difficulties in defining the scope of protected norms.
Why is the proposed introduction of the relativity requirement a proportionate and effective solution to the problem described?
Waarom is de voorgestelde invoering van het relativiteitsvereiste een evenredige en effectieve oplossing van het in de toelichting geschetste probleem is?
Accepts relativity and passing defects in principle but worries about less careful decision-making and questions the need for a large chamber.
However, the possibility of repairing a small material defect raises questions for these members.
Wel roept de mogelijkheid om een klein materieel gebrek te herstellen vragen op bij deze leden.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory opinion on the draft Wet aanpassing bestuursprocesrecht raises objections to the proposed relativity requirement, the mending of defects, incidental appeal and the large chamber, and asks for numerous amendments. The government's reply (nader rapport) accepts many points, partly follows others, and defends the relativity requirement and the extended defect-passing rule.
concerns: The Council argues the relativity requirement (art. 8:69a) may narrow legal protection to effective dispute settlement and should be reconsidered in favour of a lighter rule on third-party appeals.
The extended power to pass over defects in decisions (art. 6:22) is unclear in scope and the Council asks for clarification of its added value and boundary with art. 8:72(3).
The Council asks for clarification and adjustment of the incidental appeal rules (art. 8:104 ff.), including time limits, withdrawal and fee provisions.
The Council questions the need for a large chamber of five members and asks for convincing motivation or reconsideration.
The Council doubts the independence of persons drafting conclusions (art. 8:12a) and asks for a temporary character and adequate response period.

32522.s: The bill adds a new Article 23a to the Constitution establishing Dutch as the official language of the Netherlands, with a state duty to promote it and a enforceable individual right to use Dutch in dealings with government, subject to exceptions set by or under statute. It also includes a regulatory mandate for the legislature to regulate Frisian use and deletes two implemented additional articles of the Constitution.
32522.j: The memorandum justifies the statutory exceptions as needed for practical reasons such as diplomatic communication or service to foreigners, and states that exceptions must have a basis in formal law.
q: By or under statute, exceptions may be made to the main rule that Dutch is used in communication between government and citizen.
Bij of krachtens de wet kunnen uitzonderingen worden gegeven op de hoofdregel dat in het verkeer tussen overheid en burger het Nederlands wordt gebruikt.
d: exceptions to right to use Dutch in dealings with government
regulation of Frisian language use with government

parties: Asks whether the constitutional provision is necessary and whether citizens could enforce it against the state, e.g. migrants claiming Dutch lessons in court.
Does it not already follow from the first paragraph that everyone has the right to use Dutch when dealing with the government and to be addressed in Dutch by the government?
Vloeit uit dat eerste lid al niet voort dat een ieder het recht heeft om in het verkeer met de overheid het Nederlands te gebruiken en door de overheid in het Nederlands te worden benaderd?
Supports constitutional anchoring of Dutch but doubts the added value of the social right and asks how the duty will be concretely implemented.
They do not see how including this social fundamental right has practical added value, since the government gives no elaboration of how this right will be given effect.
Zij zien echter niet hoe de opname van dit sociaal grondrecht praktische meerwaarde heeft, nu de regering geen uitwerking geeft aan de wijze waarop dit grondrecht ingevuld zal worden.

Asks whether the provision is merely symbolic legislation linked to Islamisation and whether it will aid integration, and asks which concrete situations justify government information in other languages.
They ask whether on this point it is not merely symbolic legislation and whether this provision will actually contribute to integration.
Zij vragen zich af of op dit punt niet slechts sprake is van symboolwetgeving en of deze bepaling daadwerkelijk bij gaat dragen aan de integratie.
Welcomes the bill but wants it given concrete form in statute; asks for criteria for exceptions and warns that 'practical efficiency' exceptions to Dutch in administrative law could swallow the rule.
The administrative body is authorised to use another language when it is clear that otherwise communication with a citizen is not possible.
Het bestuursorgaan is bevoegd een andere taal te gebruiken wanneer duidelijk is dat anders niet met een burger kan worden gecommuniceerd.
Doubts the practical added value and asks why the Council of State's requirement of objective factors and necessity is met.
They share the earlier view of the Council of State that amending the Constitution should only take place if there are objective factors and a necessity for it.
Zij delen de eerdere opvatting van de Raad van State dat wijziging van de Grondwet alleen dan zou moeten plaatsvinden als daar «objectieve factoren» en een «noodzaak» voor zijn.

Questions necessity, asks whether the subjective right really protects a fundamental human right such as use of mother tongue before authorities, and worries about unequal treatment of non-Dutch speakers and restricted public information.
These members also ask the government whether a fundamental human right is not in fact at stake as well.
Deze leden vragen de regering ook, of er niet wel degelijk ook een fundamenteel mensenrecht in het geding is.
Supports the starting point but asks about scope of the government duty to promote Dutch and whether the citizen's right is already implied by paragraph 1 given the constitution's sober character.
Introducing the right to use Dutch in contact with the government is new in the Constitution.
Het invoeren van het recht om in het contact met de overheid de Nederlandse taal te gebruiken is nieuw in de Grondwet.
Positive but asks whether Dutch should be explicitly anchored as the language of the judiciary and whether the term 'government' covers courts, and why five years before entry into force.

The SGP members ask whether at least the administrative language and the language of the judiciary do not need further explicit definition to make the new constitutional provision as clear as possible.

De leden van de SGP-fractie vragen zich af of in ieder geval de bestuurstaal en de taal van de rechtspraak geen nadere explicitering nodig hebben om de nieuwe Grondwettelijke bepaling zo duidelijk mogelijk te maken.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a government bill to add a provision on Dutch as the national language to the Constitution, including a social right to promote Dutch and a subjective right to use Dutch with government, plus a regulatory mandate for Frisian. The Raad found a constitutional language clause not strictly necessary but not excluded, and advised reconsidering the official-language and social-right elements; the government replied in its nader rapport, rejecting the call to drop the social right and the classic-right terminology but accepting adjustments to the regulatory mandate and the relation to the Awb and the Halsema bill.
concerns: The Raad doubted the necessity of a constitutional language clause and asked for a stronger justification; the government supplemented the explanatory memorandum with cultural preservation and renewed societal debate as reasons.
The Raad considered calling the third paragraph a classic fundamental right inadequate; the government dropped the word classic but kept it as a subjective right.
The Raad advised dropping the social duty of the government to promote Dutch as evident and unclear in scope; the government retained it as a fundamental right of the cultural environment.

The Raad advised reconsidering the regulatory mandate on official languages, which should also cover Papiaments and English for the BES islands; the government deferred this to a later constitutional amendment.

The Raad noted that Article 2:6 Awb limits exceptions differently from the proposed third paragraph and needs adjustment; the government agreed the Awb may need amending via the transitional provision.
The Raad asked for explanation of the relation to the Halsema bill on judicial review and of the placement of the article; the government deferred comment on Halsema pending its second reading.

32531.s: The bill introduces a mandatory unpaid societal internship (maatschappelijke stage) into secondary education and amends the Wet op het voortgezet onderwijs and the Arbeidstijdenwet so that minors aged 13 and over may perform it. Implementing rules on hours, exemptions and content are left to general administrative orders (AMvB).
32531.j: The memorandum explains that detailed rules on the scope, hours and content of the internship will be set in relevant regulation, which can only be submitted to the Raad van State after the bill is adopted.
q: The proposal for elaboration in the relevant regulation can only be submitted to the Council of State once this bill has been accepted by the House of Representatives.
Het voorstel voor uitwerking in de relevante regelgeving kan overigens pas worden aangeboden aan de Raad van State als onderhavig wetsvoorstel door de Tweede Kamer is aanvaard.
d: hours and content of societal internship
rules on societal internship hours and exemptions
content of societal internship within school plan

parties: Questions the internal contradiction of a compulsory stage aimed at voluntary work and asks what concrete societal contribution and effects are demonstrated.
For the VVD members, the compulsory nature of the social internship appears to create an inner contradiction with the volunteer work it aims at.

Voor de leden van de VVD-fractie lijkt het verplichtende karakter van de maatschappelijke stage een innerlijke tegenstrijdigheid op te leveren met het vrijwilligerswerk dat de maatschappelijke stage beoogt.
Supports the stages in principle but demands they serve their purpose and do not displace vocational practical training; will test proposals against these conditions.
They therefore support introducing social internships, but find that these stages only make sense if they meet their purpose.
Zij steunen dan ook de invoering van maatschappelijke stages, maar vinden dat deze stages pas zin hebben als ze beantwoorden aan hun doel.
Welcomes the statutory anchoring and considers the stage a practical learning experience within the existing curriculum.
The statutory anchoring now taking place confirms the function of the social internship and its contribution to living together.
De wettelijke verankering die nu gaat plaats vinden is een bevestiging van de functie van de maatschappelijke stage en de bijdrage die het levert aan het met elkaar samenleven.
Positive about the idea but asks detailed questions on objectives, measurability, supervision, exemptions, and the consequences for teachers and student internship places.
They are positive about the idea behind the social internship, but do have questions about the bill.
Zij staan positief ten opzichte van het idee achter de maatschappelijke stage, maar hebben wel vragen over het wetsvoorstel.
Opposes compulsory volunteering organised by schools, arguing it burdens schools, lacks proven effect on education quality, and questions proportionality and measurable goals.
In general it is good that young people are socially involved and active, but a considerable share already do this.
Het is in zijn algemeenheid goed als jongeren maatschappelijk betrokken en actief zijn, maar een aanzienlijk deel doet dit al.
Sees the stage as valuable and asks how much freedom pupils and schools have in choosing placements, the adequacy of places, and accountability burdens.
Schools moreover have the freedom to make choices about the nature and content of the social internship.
Scholen kennen voor de invulling bovendien de vrijheid om keuzes te maken over de aard en inhoud van de maatschappelijke stage.
Argues the state should facilitate rather than compel, questions the constitutional freedom of educational means and whether compulsion exceeds the general civic mandate.
In the view of these members, the bill should facilitate without compelling.
Het wetsvoorstel dient naar de mening van deze leden te faciliteren zonder te verplichten.

v.summary: The Council of State advised on a bill introducing a compulsory social internship (maatschappelijke stage) in secondary education, questioning whether schools should carry this task, its effect on core skills and time, the vagueness of its definition, the availability of placements, the hours required, and responsibility and liability rules. The government's reply accepted a statutory definition, reduced the mandatory hours to 30 for all school types, and largely defended the policy choice while promising clarifications.
concerns: The Council questioned whether a compulsory social internship is a task for schools and whether it conflicts with the Dijsselbloem committee's call for restraint in assigning new tasks to education; the reply defended it as an implementation of existing article 17 WVO duties and added a paragraph explaining the choice.

The Council argued that counting internship hours as instruction time reduces time for basic skills and that the policy conflicts with quality goals; the reply defended the skills gained but reduced the mandatory hours to 30.
The Council advised a statutory definition of social internship and examples in the explanatory memorandum; the government added a definition to the WVO and examples.

The Council doubted there are enough suitable placements and that stage providers may be deterred by supervision responsibilities; the reply asserted sufficient placements and cited accountmanagers and partner commitments without fully resolving the concern.
The Council found the prescribed 48/60/72 hours unsubstantiated as feasible and desirable; the government reduced the requirement to 30 hours for all school types.
The Council asked why practical education students cannot be exempted under the draft article 10f; the reply explained no exemption is needed for that track and clarified the explanatory memorandum.

The Council asked for clearer allocation of responsibility and liability for internships in the explanatory memorandum; the reply pointed to existing legal allocation and added insurance to the mandatory elements of the internship agreement.

32540.s: The bill amends the Primary Education Act and the Expertise Centres Act to bring the Participatiefonds and Vervangingsfonds under the Framework Act on independent administrative bodies (Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen). It shifts public-law powers from the foundations to their boards, removes several ministerial general-direction powers in favour of policy rules, and requires the minister's approval of statutes.
32540.j: The memorandum justifies the changes by the need to align the funds with the Framework Act, stating no substantive deviations from that Act are proposed.
q: It was also indicated that no deviations from the Framework Act would be proposed.
Daarbij is tevens aangegeven dat geen afwijkingen van de Kaderwet zouden worden voorgesteld.
d: further task description, conditions for ministerial approval of statutes, consequences of withdrawing designation
p: Removes the minister's specific general-direction powers over the funds, relying instead on general policy rules under the Framework Act.
Drops the separate supervision provision, leaving supervision to the general chapter of the Framework Act.

parties: Asks why public-law tasks and oversight of public powers are given to a private-law body rather than a public-law zbo, and whether the form is appropriate.
If the minister wants to keep oversight of the exercise of public powers, the question is why a private-law independent administrative body (zbo) was chosen.
Als de minister oog wil houden op de uitoefening van publieke bevoegdheden is de vraag waarom wordt gekozen voor een privaatrechtelijk zelfstandig bestuursorgaan (zbo).
Asks what is wrong with following the Council of State's formal line on terminology and the conflict with private law, given the government's preference to keep the bill's wording.
The members ask what is wrong with following the formal line of the Council of State.
De leden vragen wat er op tegen is de formele lijn te volgen van de Raad van State.
Asks about the number of schools that signed up for a self-risk experiment for staff replacement and the government's conclusions from low participation.
They ask how many schools signed up for the experiment in which school boards would for two years fully bear the risk of replacing staff.

Zij vragen hoeveel scholen zich hebben aangemeld voor het experiment waarbij de schoolbesturen gedurende een periode van twee jaar volledig eigenrisicodrager zouden worden voor de vervanging van personeel.

v.summary: The Council of State broadly supports bringing the Vervangingsfonds and Participatiefonds under the Kaderwet zbo but objects to replacing 'de rechtspersoon' with 'het bestuur van de rechtspersoon' in the WPO and WEC, as this conflicts with private law and usual practice in special laws, and advises reverting to the legal person itself. The government replies that it distinguishes between tasks, public-law powers and private-law obligations, keeps public-law powers with the board for the reasons given, and adds the clarifications requested in the explanatory memorandum.
concerns: Replacing 'de rechtspersoon' with 'het bestuur van de rechtspersoon' creates tension with private law provisions such as the board's stated purpose and receipt of contributions; the Council advises amending the provisions so the Kaderwet applies to the legal person itself.

The Council asks that the explanatory memorandum explain the choice to keep the private-law status of the zbo's, including the relation to articles 3 and 4 of the Kaderwet and the earlier letter on rethinking the ministry's relation to the foundations.
The Council asks the explanatory memorandum to explain why the Staatssecretaris of Binnenlandse Zaken co-signs the bill rather than the Minister, under article 6 of the Kaderwet.

32603.s: The bill amends the Landbouwwet and the Meststoffenwet to rename the responsible minister and to allow the minister, by ministerial regulation, and general administrative order, to require that data be submitted exclusively electronically, with the minister able to grant exemptions. It aims to improve administrative efficiency and reduce regulatory burden.
32603.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation by saying the Awb gives no basis to require exclusively electronic submission, so a sector-specific basis is needed, and that electronic submission lowers administrative costs.
q: For that reason, article I of the amending regulation provides that entrepreneurs may be required to submit data electronically.
Om die reden is in artikel I van de wijzigingsregeling bepaald dat ondernemers verplicht kunnen worden om gegevens langs elektronische wijze te verstrekken.
d: requiring electronic submission of data and applications
ARTIKEL I B (Landbouwwet art. 25, lid 4, onderdeel b)
minister grants exemptions from electronic submission requirement
requiring electronic submission of fertiliser data
ARTIKEL II B (Meststoffenwet art. 34, lid 2, onderdeel b)
minister grants exemptions from electronic submission requirement
p: ARTIKEL I B and ARTIKEL II B

Farmers and businesses may be obliged to submit data exclusively electronically under rules set by ministerial or general administrative order, with the minister holding discretion to grant exemptions.

parties: Asks why the change must happen now rather than allowing a gradual transition, and what the exemption conditions are.
The VVD members ask why this change must happen now and why the sector cannot be given the opportunity to supply data electronically gradually.

De leden van de VVD-fractie vragen waarom deze wijziging op dit moment moet en waarom niet gewacht kan worden en de sector de gelegenheid gegeven kan worden geleidelijk elektronisch gegevens aan te leveren.
Argues the law should not enter into force until the parcel registration is repaired, the system works and everyone can comply, and raises EU audit concerns about the subsidiable area data.
The CDA members are of the view that the law can only enter into force once it is demonstrated that the whole system works and everyone can comply with it.
De leden van de CDA-fractie zijn van mening dat de wet pas inwerking kan treden als aangetoond wordt dat het gehele systeem werkt en wanneer iedereen er aan kan voldoen.
Accepts the proposal but asks how much room there is for exemption and asks the government to grant exemptions generously, noting electronic filing also has drawbacks.
They ask the government to be generous in granting exemptions.
Zij vragen de regering om ruimhartig met het verlenen van ontheffing om te springen.

32612.s: The bill adds a new title to the Dutch Code of Civil Procedure allowing lower civil courts to pose preliminary legal questions to the civil chamber of the Supreme Court in mass-claim and similar cases, with the Supreme Court able to decline to answer. It also amends the Judicial Organisation Act and court fees law and requires a report to parliament within five years.
32612.j: The memorandum justifies the procedure by faster resolution of mass claims and legal uncertainty, and by the Supreme Court's law-making role.
q: The prejudicial question to the Supreme Court in civil cases is one of the instruments by which cases can be resolved more quickly.
De prejudiciële vraag aan de Hoge Raad in civiele zaken is één van de instrumenten waarmee zaken tijdiger kunnen worden opgelost.
d: entry into force by royal decree
p: Gives lower courts a new power to refer questions to the Supreme Court, with parties heard first and a reasoned decision required.

parties: Asks whether the Supreme Court's workload will rise without safeguards, whether reformulation powers and single-judge referral are justified, and whether referral can be made binding or advisory.
Does the committee understand correctly that the current bill does not apply to the tax chamber?
Begrijpen zij het goed dat het huidige wetsvoorstel niet geldt voor de belastingkamer?
Supports faster resolution of mass damage cases but asks about cost, the Supreme Court's discretion and how third-party views are selected.
Experience with earlier mass damage cases shows their handling takes far too long, further harming victims.
De ervaringen met eerdere massaschadezaken leren dat de behandeling daarvan veel te lang duurt, wat de slachtoffers extra gedupeerd.
Asks about the scope of mass claims, how judges recognise them, and why judges need not motivate rejecting a prejudicial procedure.
These members ask why there is no duty to give reasons.
Deze leden vragen waarom er geen motiveringsplicht geldt.
Warns the procedure could let judges create quasi-legislation without legislative decision, and asks how it fits with the constitutional ban on judicial review of statutes.
One could speak here of a form of quasi-legislation.
Er kan hier worden gesproken van een vorm van pseudowetgeving.
Endorses Council of State criticism, questions the justification for a major change and warns of financial barriers and unequal access to justice.
The cuts to legal aid that the government considers necessary must in any case not be decisive in this fundamental discussion.
De naar de mening van de regering noodzakelijke bezuinigingen op rechtsbijstand mogen in ieder geval niet leidend zijn in deze principiële discussie.
Welcomes the procedure but asks about hard deadlines, parties' right to object to referral and to be heard on reformulation, and cost protection for parties.

Despite the government's stated expectation, these members ask whether it would be preferable to state explicitly in the bill that the judge does not refer a question where parties have good reason not to want it.

Ondanks de door de regering uitgesproken verwachting, vragen deze leden of het niet de voorkeur verdient om expliciet in het wetsvoorstel op te nemen dat de rechter geen prejudiciële vraag stelt, indien partijen goede reden hebben om dit niet te willen.
Questions whether the Supreme Court is the right body to encourage settlement, the breadth of 'related cases', effects on lower-court rulings, and the legal position of third-party advocates.
These members ask whether the Supreme Court is a suitable institution to promote parties reaching negotiation and settlement early.
Deze leden vragen of de Hoge Raad een geëigend instituut is om te bevorderen dat partijen vroegtijdig tot onderhandeling en schikking komen.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on a bill introducing a preliminary ruling procedure before the Dutch Supreme Court's civil chamber, raising major concerns about structural differences from ordinary cassation, the broad scope beyond mass claims, the participation of third parties, and EU-law interaction, and advising reconsideration. The minister's reply largely accepted the points, expanding justification, narrowing the scope of the extension, and amending the text, while declining to restrict third-party participation.
concerns: The Afdeling found the preliminary procedure fundamentally alters the role of the civil chamber of the Supreme Court and requires broader justification than given, which the minister partly answered by defending the proposal's rationale.

The Afdeling found no compelling reasons shown for the broad procedure and considered the extension beyond mass claims an experiment lacking a supporting motivation; the minister clarified the rationale and narrowed the definition of covered cases.
The Afdeling asked to restrict or structure the participation of third parties, which the minister rejected, leaving the Supreme Court to decide who may submit observations.
The Afdeling asked the explanatory memorandum to address the interaction with preliminary references to the EU Court of Justice following the Melki judgment, which the minister followed.
The Afdeling asked for clarification of the relationship between the proposed article 393(8) and article 81 of the Judicial Organisation Act, and redactional remarks were incorporated.

32702.s: The bill obliges any person, on demand, to provide information the public prosecutor considers necessary to enforce fines and damages measures, subject to the privilege exceptions of articles 217 and 218 Sv. It also removes the word 'periodic' from garnishment rules and drops the requirement to serve notice of garnishment on the person from whom it is taken, and makes parallel changes to the traffic enforcement act.
32702.j: The memorandum justifies the information duty by the need for effective enforcement of fines and damages, and holds that the privilege interests of articles 217 and 218 Sv must prevail over enforcement interests.
q: It is important that fines can also be recovered from these payments, so that convicted persons cannot escape fines or damages measures imposed by the judge.

Het is van belang dat geldboeten ook op deze uitkeringen kunnen worden verhaald om te zorgen dat veroordeelden niet kunnen ontkomen aan geldboeten of door de rechter opgelegde schadevergoedingsmaatregelen.
p: Public prosecutor may compel any person to provide information it deems necessary for enforcing fines, subject only to the prosecutor's own reasonableness judgment and privilege exceptions.
Removes the requirement to serve written notice of garnishment on the person from whom the amount is taken, reducing that person's notice protection.
Extends the same compelled information duty to traffic administrative sanctions, with the prosecutor deciding what information is necessary.

parties: Asks whether refusing to comply with the prosecutor's information demands on the new obligations is also punishable under article 184 Sr.
Asks whether information demands are limited to what enforcement needs, whether a payment arrangement is possible when debtors fall below subsistence level, and how the CJIB will handle this.
The PvdA members ask to what extent the convicted person's ability to pay is taken into account when collecting the monetary sanction.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie vragen in hoeverre bij het innen van de geldsanctie rekening wordt gehouden met de draagkracht van de veroordeelde.
Asks why information duties are limited to what is needed for enforcement and why they apply only to persons in the Netherlands.
These members ask the government why this limitation has been included.
Deze leden vragen de regering waarom deze beperking is opgenomen.
Endorses the balance between prosecution needs and privacy, but asks whether proportionality applies to the wider circle of persons who can be approached and how the balancing is done and by whom.
That demand must be limited to the information necessary for enforcing the sanction.
Die vordering moet beperkt blijven tot het vorderen van die inlichtingen die noodzakelijk zijn voor de tenuitvoerlegging van de sanctie.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that a bill combining electronic applications for certificates of good conduct with rules on providing information to the public prosecution service for enforcing fines contained unrelated subjects, and recommended splitting it into two bills. The government's reply states it followed this advice by splitting the bill and making minor drafting changes.
concerns: The Afdeling found insufficient substantive coherence between the subjects in the bill and advised splitting it into two separate bills.

32710-IIB.s: The bill amends the 2010 departmental budget statements of the Raad van State, Algemene Rekenkamer, Nationale ombudsman, Kanselarij der Nederlandse Orden and the governors' cabinets of the Netherlands Antilles and Aruba, following the supplementary and closing budget adjustments. It is a budgetary adjustment law that makes no changes to executive powers, delegations or oversight arrangements.
q: The present bill aims to make changes for the year 2010 to the departmental budget statements of the Raad van State, the Algemene Rekenkamer, the Nationale ombudsman, the Kanselarij der Nederlandse Orden, the Cabinet of the Governor of the Netherlands Antilles and the Cabinet of the Governor of Aruba (IIB).

Het onderhavige wetsvoorstel strekt ertoe om voor het jaar 2010 wijzigingen aan te brengen in de departementale begrotingsstaat van de Raad van State, de Algemene Rekenkamer, de Nationale ombudsman, de Kanselarij der Nederlandse Orden, het Kabinet van de Gouverneur van de Nederlandse Antillen en het Kabinet van de Gouverneur van Aruba (IIB).

32711.s: The bill amends the Dutch organ donation act to replace the term 'intreden van de dood' with 'vaststellen van de dood' and to allow preparatory medical steps before death in potential donors who have no declared wish. It also lets nearest relatives give substitute consent for persons who were incapable of reasoned judgment and allows an administrative measure to exempt categories of doctors from certain rules.
32711.j: The memorandum justifies the changes by new medical-technical possibilities, practical confusion over the term 'intreden van de dood', and consultation with professional associations to ensure legal certainty and workability.
q: This amendment of article 22 thus legitimises such preparations from the moment the prognosis is infaust and continuing them would be medically pointless for the person concerned.
Deze wijziging van artikel 22 legitimeert zulke voorbereidingen dus vanaf het moment dat de prognose infaust is en voortzetting ervan voor betrokkene zelf medisch zinloos zou zijn.
d: exempting categories of doctors from article 20 rules
p: Allows preparations for organ removal before death once prognosis is infaust, narrowing the consent requirement and personal bodily integrity protection, subject to listed conditions.
Permits substitute consent by relatives after death for persons who were never capable of reasoned judgment about organ donation.

parties: Asks that relatives be reached and involved before any preparatory steps, so that self-determination and a real choice for relatives is preserved.
As far as these members are concerned, the proposed bill must therefore not lead to delay, for whatever reason, in the conversation with relatives about organ donation.
Voorliggend wetsvoorstel mag wat deze leden betreft dan ook niet leiden tot uitstel – om wat voor reden dan ook – van het gesprek met nabestaanden over orgaandonatie.
Asks which preparatory steps are permitted, whether the list is exhaustive, and how the consequences of not choosing are communicated to citizens.
Can the government indicate how it intends to bring the consequences of 'not choosing' to people's attention through public information?
Kan de regering aangeven op welke wijze zij de consequenties van het «niet kiezen» via voorlichting onder de aandacht van de mensen wil brengen?
Asks for clear limits on preparatory steps, whether relatives know they can object at any time, and that relatives' interests are not overshadowed.
Solving practical problems must not mean that the interests of relatives recede into the background.
Het oplossen van praktische problemen mag niet betekenen dat de belangen van nabestaanden op de achtergrond raken.
Supports the change in principle but demands careful justification of any infringement on bodily integrity under Article 11 of the Constitution and asks for detail on the preparatory acts.
Every infringement must of course be very carefully justified.
Elke inbreuk moet uiteraard zeer zorgvuldig worden onderbouwd.
Asks whether the new 'no objection' element increases pressure on relatives and whether it is truly necessary to limit bodily integrity and self-determination.
These members ask whether the added 'no objection' element will put more pressure on relatives to reach a choice on whether to consent to donation.
Deze leden vragen of door het inbouwen van dit extra «geen bezwaar»-element meer druk op de nabestaanden wordt gelegd om tot een keuze te komen om wel of geen toestemming te geven voor donatie.

Insists explicit consent remain essential and asks why relatives are not brought in when the patient cannot consent; questions the justification for infringing bodily integrity for third-party benefit.
The SGP members consider it essential that explicit consent remains required in all cases.
De leden van de SGP-fractie vinden het essentieel dat er in alle gevallen sprake blijft van expliciete toestemming.

v.summary: The Raad van State advises that the bill amending the Organ Donation Act, which would allow preparatory acts for donation before death without the patient's or relatives' consent, be revised to clarify necessity, subsidiarity and proportionality under Article 11 of the Constitution. The government's reply (nader rapport) accepts the advice in part, adds a narrowed and clarified provision on permitted preparatory acts, rejects the request to put the consequence on the donor form, and adjusts the drafting.
concerns: Preparatory acts for donation before death without consent may infringe bodily integrity and self-determination under Article 11 of the Constitution, requiring stronger justification and analysis.

The bill must show a balancing of the need for organs against the donor's and relatives' interests, and whether less intrusive alternatives exist, in light of necessity, subsidiarity and proportionality.
Article 22(3) wrongly implies that permitted pre-death preparatory acts must stop for five minutes after cardiac arrest, and the provisions should be clarified and restructured.

The Raad advises stating the consequence of non-registration (preparatory acts permitted before relatives decide) on the donor form, which the government declines to do, relying on a separate cover letter and website.

32810.s: This omnibus tax bill (Fiscale verzamelwet 2011) makes many technical and redactional amendments to tax laws, including updating ministry names, repairing erroneous cross-references, and correcting omitted delegations. It also adds or extends delegation powers allowing lower-level regulations and ministerial rules to set reporting obligations, relief conditions and refund rules.
32810.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as needed to fix omitted or erroneous delegation bases and to specify reporting details for the pre-filled tax return, without changing substance.
q: To make this extension possible, adequate delegation power must be included in the Income Tax Act 2001.
Om deze uitbreiding te kunnen bewerkstelligen dient een toereikende delegatiebevoegdheid te worden opgenomen in de Wet inkomstenbelasting 2001.
d: Artikel I, onderdeel BB (art. 10.8 Wet IB 2001)
time limits and manner for third-party data reporting to tax inspector
Artikel III, onderdeel A (art. 11 Wet LB 1964)
designating military war and service victim benefits as exempt
Artikel III, onderdeel H (art. 31a Wet LB 1964)
groups of employees and conditions for extraterritorial cost allowances
Artikel IX, onderdeel G (art. 59 Wet belastingen op milieugrondslag)
further rules for application of environmental tax provisions
Artikel XIV, onderdelen A en B (art. 37, 38 AWR)
rules to prevent double taxation, now with subdelegation possible
Artikel XXII, onderdeel B (art. 8.121 Belastingwet BES)
rules to prevent double taxation in the Caribbean Netherlands, with subdelegation
Artikel XXIII, onderdeel D (art. 4.50a Douane- en Accijnswet BES)
conditions and restrictions for excise refund on goods shipped abroad
Artikel XXIII, onderdeel D (art. 4.50a, tweede lid Douane- en Accijnswet BES)
Artikel XVI (art. 30, achtste lid Wet waardering onroerende zaken)
joint regulation may designate municipal officials for valuation tasks
p: Expands the inspector's power to recover erroneously paid refunds, with a five-year limitation period as a constraint.

parties: Asks the government to explain why it did not follow the Raad van State's advice on the delegation-power repair.
The VVD members read that the Council of State advises repairing the delegation power in a different way than the method proposed in the bill.

De leden van de VVD-fractie lezen dat de Raad van State adviseert om een reparatie met betrekking tot delegatiebevoegdheid op een andere wijze te regelen dan door middel van de in het wetsvoorstel voorgestelde methode.
Argues that correcting legislative errors must follow the rules of the game, and that a retroactive delegation power and appeal to legislative economy are insufficient justification.
An appeal to 'legislative economy' is not sufficient here, even for economists.
Een beroep op «wetgevingseconomie» is hier – zelfs voor economen – niet voldoende.
Asks whether self-standing ministerial regulations without adequate delegation basis exist in tax law, which is generally undesirable.
The existence of 'self-standing ministerial regulations' is generally regarded as an undesirable situation.
Het bestaan van «zelfstandige ministeriële regelingen» wordt over het algemeen beschouwd als een onwenselijke situatie.
Has no questions on the bill apart from a point raised by the NOB on alimony as debt in box 3.
The members have no questions about this proposal, except regarding a point raised by the Dutch Order of Tax Advisers (NOB).
De leden hebben geen vragen over dit voorstel, behalve ten aanzien van een punt opgebracht door de Nederlandse Orde van Belastingadviseurs (NOB).
Accepts the proposed repair of unintended effects on Vamil buildings from the gradual abolition of box 3 exemptions.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on the Fiscal Omnibus Act 2011, objecting to retroactive extension of the animal-related tax provisions (broader scope than the withdrawn Regeling agressieve dieren) and to retroactive delegation powers. The government's reply accepted the animal-provisions point by limiting retroactivity via a new article XXV, and kept its method for the delegation repair for legislative economy while making redactional changes.
concerns: Retroactive extension of animal-related tax provisions broadens tax burden without the exceptional circumstances justifying retroactivity; government limited retroactivity to animals covered by the former regulation via article XXV.

A delegation power cannot be introduced retroactively; the Afdeling advised allowing retroactive regulations instead, but the government kept its retroactive delegation method for legislative economy.
Several redactional comments on wording, delegation formulation and ministry names were followed.

33000-III.s: This bill sets the 2012 budget statements for the Ministry of General Affairs (including the Dienst Publiek en Communicatie service agency), the Cabinet of the Queen, and the Commission for oversight of the intelligence and security services (CTIVD), in thousands of euros. It enters into force on 1 January 2012 and contains no delegation of rule-making power or shifts of power to the executive.
q: The present articles aim to establish the budget statements of the Ministry of General Affairs, the Cabinet of the Queen and the Commission for oversight of the intelligence and security services for the year 2012.

De onderhavige wetsartikelen strekken ertoe om de begrotingsstaten van respectievelijk het Ministerie van Algemene Zaken, van het Kabinet der Koningin en van de Commissie van toezicht betreffende de inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten voor het jaar 2012 vast te stellen.

33008.s: The bill amends the Dutch Criminal Code and related youth-justice laws on the placement of young offenders (PIJ measure), mainly to simplify mandatory aftercare by removing mandatory judicial involvement when the youth complies, and by letting the court set the duration of extensions and returns to custody with a cap of one year. It also adds a right to appeal against ministerial refusal or withdrawal of a STP training-programme permit and makes some changes retroactive.
33008.j: The memorandum justifies removing mandatory judicial involvement as simplifying the young scheme and reducing unnecessary bureaucracy, as the mandatory aftercare regime is still new.
q: For cases where aftercare proceeds as desired and the youth follows reclassering's directions, the bill proposes to drop the mandatory judicial intervention.

Voor die gevallen waarin de nazorg naar wens verloopt en de jeugdige zich gedraagt naar de aanwijzingen van de reclassering, wordt voorgesteld de verplichte rechterlijke tussenkomst te laten vervallen.
p: Removes the mandatory judicial decision within three to six months after conditional release, so the youth's conditional discharge can run without court review when the youth complies with reclassering supervision.
Allows the court to order that a placement in a youth institution is not executed, giving the judiciary discretion in sentence execution.
Gives the youth a right of appeal against a ministerial decision on STP permits, including failure to decide in time and withdrawal of a permit, strengthening legal protection.

parties: Asks whether the cap on re-detention guarantees youths return to society after a resocialisation track and where the limit lies after repeated relapses.
These members ask whether it can be said with certainty that the youth with a PIJ measure is always returned to society after a resocialisation track.
Deze leden vragen of met zekerheid gezegd kan worden dat de jeugdige met een pij-maatregel altijd na een resocialisatietraject terug in de maatschappij wordt geplaatst.
Asks why 'time-out' re-placement is limited to two times and whether the judge can impose new or tightened conditions afterwards.
They ask why it was chosen to apply the 'time-out' at most twice.
Zij vragen waarom is gekozen voor het ten hoogste tweemaal toepassen van de «time-out.»
Questions the removal of judicial involvement when aftercare goes well and asks whether the time-out's temporary character should be made explicit in the law.
Regarding the removal of judicial involvement in ending the PIJ measure when aftercare has gone as hoped, these members ask why it was initially proposed to give the judge a role in this.

Met betrekking tot het schrappen van de rechterlijke tussenkomst bij het eindigen van de pij-maatregel indien de nazorg naar wens is verlopen, vragen deze leden waarom aanvankelijk werd voorgesteld de rechter hierin wel een rol te geven.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill amending the Criminal Code to close a gap in the conditional termination of the PIJ measure (placement of juveniles), concerning mandatory aftercare. The Afdeling asked that the maximum duration of re-placement be aligned with the remaining term of the conditional termination, and the minister's reply added a sentence stating that re-placement cannot exceed that term and limited re-placements to two, plus a drafting correction.
concerns: Re-placement duration must not exceed the remaining period of conditional termination and thus the measure's duration, given retroactive effect and possible increased severity.
A cross-reference to article 1 of the Wet op de jeugdzorg needed correction to match the amended provision.

33017.s: The bill abolishes the municipal power to establish borough councils (deelgemeenten) by repealing the Gemeentewet provisions on them and removing related references in several other laws. It also makes consequential amendments to the Provinciewet, Waterschapswet, Wet openbare lichamen Bonaire, Sint Eustatius en Saba, pension, traffic and social insurance laws.
33017.j: The memorandum justifies the abolition as part of a policy of a small, service-oriented government with fewer officials, rules and administrators, and argues that borough councils no longer meet the criteria of a general representative body under Article 4 of the Constitution.
q: The purpose of this bill is to abolish the power of municipal governments to establish borough councils (deelgemeenten).
Strekking van dit wetsvoorstel is het afschaffen van de bevoegdheid van gemeentebesturen om deelgemeenten in te stellen.
p: Repeals the statutory basis for municipal borough councils with directly elected representatives, removing a subnational layer of representative government and its autonomy-based constitutional position.

parties: Asks how the replacement commissions can fulfil participation and service functions without elections, and whether elections should remain possible.
But for matters such as participation and involvement, administrative deconcentration and service delivery to citizens, elections are not necessary and it is possible to establish commissions.
Maar voor zaken als inspraak en betrokkenheid, ambtelijke deconcentratie en serviceverlening aan burgers zijn verkiezingen niet nodig en is er de mogelijkheid commissies in te stellen.
Criticises the government for piecemeal reform and asks for a broadly supported vision before concrete measures, and questions the loss of closeness between government and citizens.
Therefore these members want to propose that the government first conduct the discussion on the vision of administrative organisation and on that basis work out the concrete measures.
Daarom willen deze leden de regering voorstellen om eerst de discussie te voeren over de visie op de bestuurlijke inrichting en op basis daarvan de concrete maatregelen uit te werken.
Asks whether the organisation of commissions is for the municipality to decide and how the financial consequences and workload for Amsterdam and Rotterdam councillors will be handled.
Does the government share the view of the CDA members that the organisation and staffing of commissions under article 83 of the Municipalities Act is a matter for the municipality?
Deelt de regering de opvatting van de leden van de CDA-fractie, dat de inrichting en de bemensing van bestuurscommissies ex artikel 83 van de Gemeentewet een zaak is van de gemeente?
Doubts the bill will make government more transparent and asks how democratic control over the local administration is ensured after the change.
Even if a number of administrators formally take on the role of civil servant, good democratic control over the administration remains necessary.
Ook als een aantal bestuurders formeel de rol van ambtenaar krijgt, blijft een goede democratische controle op het bestuur noodzakelijk.
Argues the reform is premature without a metropolitan vision and asks what safeguards prevent replacement commissions from becoming de facto sub-municipal bodies without democratic legitimacy.
What safeguards does the government have to prevent the administrative commissions from eventually becoming de facto sub-municipal councils without democratic legitimacy?
Welke waarborgen heeft de regering om te voorkomen dat de bestuurlijke commissies op termijn niet uitgroeien tot de facto deelgemeenten, zonder democratische legitimatie?
Objects that abolishing deelgemeenten erodes democratic control and local autonomy, that the Council of State found the justification insufficient, and asks about local support.
The Council of State also indicates that the government's justification is insufficiently convincing.
Ook de Raad van State geeft aan dat de motivering van de regering onvoldoende overtuigt.
Objects to the bill for lacking adequate justification and asks how it is compatible with municipal autonomy and whether the alternatives guarantee equivalent democratic control.
Asks whether citizens' involvement in local government is better safeguarded through elected commissions than through deelgemeenten and what the consequences are for service quality.
Is citizens' involvement in local government, including through elections in the commissions, better guaranteed than in deelgemeenten?
Is de betrokkenheid van burgers bij het lokale bestuur door onder meer verkiezingen bij de bestuurscommissies op een betere manier gewaarborgd dan bij deelgemeenten?

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the bill abolishing the municipal power to establish deelgemeenten but raises objections on local autonomy, the scope of territorial committees, and financial consequences, advising adaptation. The government's nader rapport rejects most objections, defends the bill as an effective step toward a compact state, and clarifies the financial consequences, while making a few textual adjustments.
concerns: The Afdeling argues that abolishing deelgemeenten restricts municipal autonomy without a sufficient reasoned justification, and advises waiting for the planned vision on domestic governance.
The Afdeling doubts whether the bill will effectively achieve a smaller government, since municipalities may still create territorial committees with substantial tasks.
The Afdeling contends that under the Article 4 Grondwet case law, territorial committees with substantial tasks would require direct elections, and that the bill revives the pre-1994 situation.

The Afdeling asks for a fuller explanation of the financial consequences for Amsterdam and Rotterdam under the Financiële-verhoudingswet; the government maintains the explanation suffices but removes a sentence on who bears reorganisation costs.
