33062.s: The bill requires a range of public institutions, professionals and self-employed practitioners (justice youth institutions, prisons, TBS institutions, education, childcare, health care, municipal services, the health service) to adopt and promote a meldcode (reporting code) for domestic violence and child abuse. It also creates municipal Steunpunten Huiselijk Geweld as reporting points, with rights to process sensitive personal data and to share information without consent, subject to safeguards.
33062.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations by saying the detailed elements of the meldcode and the municipal arrangements are best set by general administrative order, to fit existing practice and sector-specific needs.
q: By or pursuant to a general administrative order it is determined which elements a meldcode must at least contain.
Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur wordt vastgesteld uit welke elementen een meldcode in ieder geval bestaat.
d: Artikel I/II/III/XI/XIV/XV (5 lid) and related provisions
working method and required expertise of Steunpunt Huiselijk Geweld
designation of municipalities required to organise a Steunpunt
rules on when the identity of a reporter may be withheld
Artikel XIII, Wet BIG, artikel 40a lid 4
elements of meldcode for individual health care professionals
p: Artikel XII, Wmo, artikel 21c lid 2-3 and 21d-21g

Steunpunten may process sensitive personal data and professionals may disclose information without consent, with access and notification rights to citizens limited for the purpose of investigating domestic violence.
The Steunpunt may omit notifying data subjects of collection of their data where needed to investigate domestic violence.

parties: Asks how compliance with the meldcode is monitored by supervisors and the municipality, and whether all sector codes meet the minimum requirements.
Do supervisors, for example, check whether all these different meldcodes meet the minimum requirements?
Wordt door bijvoorbeeld de toezichthouders bekeken of al deze verschillende meldcodes voldoen aan de minimumeisen?
Supports the code but questions capacity of AMKs and SHGs and the lack of structural funding for forensic child abuse examination; asks about recidivism of offenders.
These members find it unacceptable that child abuse and domestic violence still occur on a large scale in the Netherlands.
Deze leden achten het onacceptabel dat kindermishandeling en huiselijk geweld in Nederland nog steeds op grote schaal voorkomt.
Supports a statutory duty to adopt a code, asks for prior submission (voorhang) of the AMvBs, an evaluation clause, and clarity on enforcement and legal consequences for professionals.
These members request prior submission (voorhang) of these general administrative orders (AMvBs).
Genoemde leden verzoeken de regering om voorhang van deze algemene maatregelen van bestuur (amvb’s).

Objects that only 10% of professionals will be trained despite the Langkamp motion requiring training for all; raises the dual-consent problem for examinations and whether the code can become a repressive control tool.
These members are very surprised and express their dissatisfaction that the bill states only 10% of professionals will be trained.
Genoemde leden zijn zeer verbaasd en spreken hun ongenoegen uit over het feit dat in het wetsvoorstel staat dat slechts 10% van de professionals geschoold zal worden.
Asks how application of the code is supervised in municipalities, how over-reporting and under-reporting are prevented, and requests clearer legal responsibility and liability.
Supports the code and the absence of a reporting duty, asks about expected output, training needs, and the relation to the verwijsindex risicojongeren.
These members are convinced that establishing a mandatory meldcode contributes to preventing, detecting, stopping and limiting harm from abuse as much as possible.
Deze leden zijn ervan overtuigd dat het instellen van een verplichte meldcode bijdraagt aan het zo veel mogelijk voorkomen, signaleren, stoppen en beperken van op te lopen schade bij mishandeling.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised, in its opinion of 3 August 2011, that the bill mandating a domestic violence and child abuse reporting code (meldcode) for professionals and organisations needs further consideration, raising concerns about the added value of a legal obligation, the scope of reporting powers, the capacity of the steunpunten huiselijk geweld and the AMK, and the processing of special personal data without consent. The government's nader rapport of 24 October 2011 largely accepts the points, clarifying the explanatory memorandum, narrowing the Wmo powers, and adjusting the text.
concerns: The Council doubts a statutory obligation to adopt a meldcode is necessary given voluntary uptake, and the government maintains it is necessary while adding clarification on side effects.

The Council warns a mandatory meldcode may pressure professionals into unnecessary reporting and creates liability risks, which the explanatory memorandum did not address; the government sharpened the text but disputes the pressure concern.
The Council flags the undefined term professional and the scope of covered personnel, which the government clarified in the memorandum.

The Council questions whether steunpunten and the AMK have the capacity and expertise for expanded tasks and powers; the government points to a subsidy programme and reserved funds but leaves amounts to be agreed.

The Council advises limiting the Wmo powers to process special personal data without consent to cases involving only adults and aligning the scope with the Wet op de jeugdzorg; the government kept the powers for steunpunten, reasoning that combined child and adult cases need them, but tightened the wording.
The Council asks that the wording of the Wmo third paragraph align with the Wet op de jeugdzorg standard of a reasonable suspicion of child abuse, and the government amended it.

33071.s: The bill raises court filing fees (griffierechten) in administrative and civil law, introducing a tiered fee structure with reduced rates for low and middle incomes and a hardship clause. It also makes administrative bodies pay a fee to the court when they lose a case, and widens the court's discretion over cost awards.
33071.j: The memorandum justifies higher fees as a fair share of court costs for users and a necessary budget measure, and says the lower-income reductions and hardship clauses protect access to justice.
q: The cabinet considers it justified that users of the judiciary in those 5% of civil and administrative disputes – subject to exceptions – make a higher contribution to the costs of these proceedings.

Het kabinet vindt het gerechtvaardigd dat gebruikers van de rechtspraak in die 5% van de civiele en bestuursrechtelijke geschillen – behoudens uitzonderingen – een hogere bijdrage leveren in de kosten van deze procedures.
d: annual indexation of income thresholds for reduced fees
annual adjustment of income thresholds and fee amounts
Wet op de Raad van State, article 51 (13)
amendment of appeal fees by general administrative order
Beroepswet, article 22 (14); Wet bestuursrechtspraak bedrijfsorganisatie, article 24 (13)
amendment of appeal fees by general administrative order
annual indexation of income thresholds for civil fee reductions
p: Artikel 8:41a Awb; judicial discretion clauses (8:41a(9), 8:109(3), Wgbz 16, 127a Rv)
Courts may waive or reduce fees for lack of financial means where payment would cause unfairness, a safeguard for citizens' access to court.
Court may limit cost awards against a losing party to the fee that party paid, where full award would be unfair.
Artikel 8:74, 8:84, 8:86 Awb (fees payable by administrative bodies)
Administrative bodies must pay court fees to the court when they lose, creating a cost for public authorities that may discourage unnecessary litigation.

parties: Supports compensation for low-income litigants and access to justice under Article 6 ECHR, while asking whether no-cure-no-pay arrangements could be developed to protect access to courts.
The right of access to a court, under Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights, must be guaranteed.
Het recht op toegang tot de rechter, conform artikel 6 Europees Verdrag tot bescherming van de Rechten van de Mens en de Fundamentele Vrijheden (EVRM), dient gewaarborgd te worden.
Argues the fee increases disproportionately worsen access to the courts, deter citizens from challenging government decisions, and could embolden authorities and businesses.
In the view of these members, those fundamentals are at stake when access to the courts is disproportionately worsened by the proposed fee increases.

Naar de mening van voornoemde leden zijn die in het geding op het moment dat de toegankelijkheid van de rechter disproportioneel wordt verslechterd door de voorgenomen verhogingen van de griffierechten.
Notes the bill is necessary and asks the government to monitor that access to the courts remains sufficient.
These members therefore support compensation for low-income persons, but ask the government to keep a close watch on this and ensure access to the courts remains sufficient.

Voornoemde leden onderschrijven daarom de compensatie van on- en minvermogenden, maar verzoeken de regering dit goed in de gaten te blijven houden en te zorgen dat toegang tot de rechter wel in voldoende mate aanwezig blijft.
Supports user contributions and alternatives to litigation, but raises concern that high fees for defendants may conflict with Article 6 ECHR and Article 47 of the EU Charter.
Although the bill has been considerably improved in response to criticism from the field, these members want to address this point explicitly in this written contribution.

Weliswaar is het wetsvoorstel naar aanleiding van de kritiek uit het veld aanzienlijk verbeterd, maar deze leden hebben er wel behoefte aan om dit punt in deze schriftelijke inbreng expliciet te adresseren.
Argues higher fees penalise citizens who seek justice, that courts serve a collective public interest, and that the reduction in cases may conflict with constitutional and ECHR access guarantees.
The members of the SP faction are of the view that anyone compelled to turn to the courts is in effect punished.
De leden van de SP-fractie zijn van mening dat een ieder die genoodzaakt wordt zich tot de rechter te wenden als het ware wordt gestraft.
Calls the bill highly controversial, warns about access to the courts, and questions whether court costs should rest on users given the wider societal value of case law.
The greatest concern is the effect of the bill on the accessibility of the judiciary.
Grootste zorg is het effect van het wetsvoorstel op de toegankelijkheid van de rechtspraak.
Stresses the judiciary as a collective good and questions whether the risk of high cost orders against losing less wealthy parties deters bringing disputes to court.
These members ask whether the risk of a high costs order does not form a disproportionate barrier to bringing a dispute before the court.
Deze leden vragen of het risico van een hoge proceskostenveroordeling niet een onevenredige drempel vormt op om een geschil aan de rechter voor te leggen.
Asks whether access to the law is preserved, whether fees may exceed case costs, and whether restraint is needed in administrative cases to protect citizens against arbitrary government.
Protection of citizens against arbitrariness by the government requires restraint in the level of court fees, particularly in administrative law.
Bescherming van de burger tegen willekeur door de overheid noodzaakt in het bijzonder bij het bestuursrecht tot terughoudendheid bij de hoogte van de griffierechten.

v.summary: The Council of State's Advisory Division advised on 15 September 2011 against positive advice on a bill raising court fees to cover costs of civil and administrative justice, citing the constitutional function of the judiciary, access to justice, cumulative fees and missing hardship clause. The minister's reply of 28 October 2011 accepted several points (hardship clause added, lower tariffs for administrative cases, no fee for government appellees) but kept the cost-recovery approach.
concerns: Access to the court may be made illusory by the substantial fee increases, violating Article 6 ECHR and Article 47 EU Charter; the minister disputes this but lowered administrative fees and kept the rest.

The judiciary is a constitutionally anchored collective good whose cost should be borne by the whole legal community; the minister acknowledges its importance but rejects its economic framing as decisive.
Cumulative fees across procedural stages and the proportionality of higher fees to the legitimate aim were insufficiently justified; the minister added explanation but largely defended the design.
The bill lacked a hardship clause (hardheidsclausule), which the minister added to the relevant articles.
Government appellees in administrative appeal should not be charged fees for defending against a higher appeal; the minister dropped this charge.
Third parties in administrative appeal should not pay fees for submitting their views on appeal; the minister clarified they are exempt.
Financial effects of the 240 million euro saving, including refunds and deterred filings, were unclear; the minister explained the model and parameters.
Rules for provisional fee assessment without a statement of income and for additional payments create practical enforcement problems; the minister aligned the rules with civil law.
The bill's structure depended on a pending bill, risking textual conflicts; a savings clause was added and the bill renamed.

33107.s: The bill amends the Wet arbeid en zorg to add a protection against detriment for employees who claim or assist with parental leave rights, implementing Directive 2010/18/EU. It also adds a provision to the Arbeidstijdenwet letting employees request a temporary adjustment of their working-time pattern after parental leave, with fixed request and decision deadlines that collective agreements may deviate from.
33107.j: The memorandum justifies the collective-agreement deviation option by the directive's allowance for social partners to adapt provisions to sector and company circumstances.
q: The second and third paragraphs may be deviated from by collective regulation.
Van het tweede en derde lid kan worden afgeweken bij collectieve regeling.
d: Artikel I (Artikel 6:1a Wet arbeid en zorg)
collective agreements may deviate from request and decision rules for working-time adjustment
collective regulation may deviate from timing requirements for requests and decisions

parties: Asks what 'small enterprises' means and how the directive's detriment protection and the temporary adjustment of working patterns are implemented, stressing room for social partners to tailor rules.

The VVD members stress that (European) regulation should only sketch the frameworks and that enough room must remain for national member states, but above all for the social partners, to make arrangements that fit their own situation.

De leden van de VVD-fractie benadrukken dat (Europese) regelgeving slechts de kaders dient te schetsen en dat er voldoende ruimte moet blijven voor de nationale lidstaten, maar vooral voor de sociale partners, om regelingen te treffen, die aansluiten bij de eigen situatie.
Opposes EU involvement in social policy as European meddling and asks who decides when detrimental treatment occurs and whether deadlines can be shortened by collective agreement.

The PVV members note that the bill proposes a derogation power, namely that a collective agreement may deviate from the obligation to request an adjustment of working patterns three months in advance.*)

De leden van de PVV-fractie constateren dat het onderhavige wetsvoorstel een afwijkingsbevoegdheid voorstelt, namelijk dat bij collectieve regeling kan worden afgeweken van de verplichting om drie maanden van tevoren te verzoeken om aanpassing van het arbeidspatroon.
Asks about the criteria employers must apply when assessing adjustment requests, about protection against detriment, and whether more favourable national rules were considered.
These members note that the directive allows member states to adopt more favourable provisions.*)
Deze leden constateren dat in de richtlijn de mogelijkheid bestaat voor lidstaten om gunstigere bepalingen vast te stellen.
Argues unpaid parental leave deters low-income families and asks whether paid leave will be introduced and how adoption leave can be extended.
Is the government willing to introduce paid parental leave?*)
Is de regering bereid om betaald ouderschapsverlof in te voeren?
Asks why the one-year employment threshold was chosen and whether social partners were consulted on adoption leave.
These members ask whether the social partners were consulted on adoption leave.*)
Deze leden vragen of de sociale partners zijn geconsulteerd over het adoptieverlof.

33116.s: The bill creates a general experimentation clause in the primary, special secondary, secondary and Caribbean education acts, allowing deviation from statutory provisions by general administrative order for innovation experiments of up to six years. It also allows experimental cooperation between schools and institutions across education sectors and makes related technical amendments.
33116.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation by the need for faster, flexible innovation across education sectors, with safeguards such as the general administrative order form, a six-year limit, evaluation and parliamentary reporting.
q: Thus deviation from the statute for an experiment can only be arranged by general administrative order, and the duration of such an experiment is limited.
Zo geldt dat afwijking van de wet ten behoeve van een experiment alleen maar bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kan worden geregeld en dat de duur van zo'n experiment beperkt is.
d: Artikel I (new art. 176k WPO), eerste lid
deviation from statutory provisions for primary education experiments
Artikel I (new art. 176k WPO), derde lid
Artikel I (new art. 176k WPO), zevende lid
rules applying to school cooperation experiments
Artikel II (new art. 145a WPO BES), eerste lid
deviation from statutory provisions for Caribbean primary education experiments
Artikel III (new art. 171 WEC), eerste lid
deviation from statutory provisions for special education experiments
Artikel IV (new art. 118t WVO), eerste lid
deviation from statutory provisions for secondary education experiments
Artikel IV (new art. 118t WVO), zesde lid
deviation from compulsory schooling, fee and student finance laws for experiments
Artikel V (new art. 205a WVO BES), eerste lid
deviation from statutory provisions for Caribbean secondary education experiments
p: Artikel I (new art. 176k WPO), eerste lid
Allows the government by general administrative order to depart from numerous statutory provisions for innovation experiments, subject to a pre-submission period and a six-year limit.
Artikel I (new art. 176k WPO), vierde lid
Allows the minister to extend an experiment beyond six years while a bill converting it into permanent law is pending.
Artikel II, III, IV, V (experiment articles)
Parallel experimentation clauses in the other education acts give the executive similar power to set aside statutory education rules.

parties: Asks how experiments are supervised by the inspectorate, whether they can be stopped early, and how 'organisatie' fits as a criterion.
Does the education inspectorate supervise the experiments, the members ask, and if so, how will it do so?
Houdt de inspectie van het onderwijs toezicht op de experimenten, vragen deze leden, en zo ja, hoe zal zij dit doen?
Sees the bill as a step forward but questions whether it goes far enough, and raises principles of general access, teacher qualification and the role of government.
They do wonder, however, whether more could and should be done in this direction.
Zij vragen zich echter af of er niet nog wat verder kan en moet worden gegaan.
Very positive about innovative experimental space to improve education quality.
The members are very positive about the possibility of innovative experimental space in education to improve quality.
De leden staan zeer positief tegenover mogelijkheid voor innovatieve experimenteerruimte in het onderwijs ten behoeve van kwaliteitsverbetering in het onderwijs.
Welcomes a firmer legal basis for successful experiments and asks the cabinet to quickly issue a general administrative order (AMvB) and clarify plans.

The aforementioned members ask the cabinet, taking into account the 10-point plan the CDA submitted during the budget debate, to come as soon as possible with a general administrative order (AMvB) to this effect.

De voornoemde leden vragen het kabinet om, met inachtneming van het 10-puntenplan dat de CDA-fractie tijdens de begroting heeft ingediend, zo spoedig mogelijk met een algemene maatregel van bestuur (AMvB) met deze strekking te komen.
Supports room to experiment but asks about the role of the Chamber, whether experiments can be blocked, duration limits, teacher qualification, tuition barriers and consultation.
They ask whether all experiments are explicitly submitted to the Chamber and how it can amend or block them when it deems necessary.
Zij vragen of alle experimenten expliciet worden voorgelegd aan de Kamer en hoe zij deze kan aanpassen of blokkeren wanneer zij dat nodig acht.
Recognises potential benefits but worries about the autonomy of school boards and parents' say, external pressure in shrinking regions, and the role of the Chamber.
The members do, however, have concerns about the say of individual school boards and of parents regarding this amendment on experiments in their education sector or region.
De leden hebben echter wel zorgen over de zeggenschap van individuele schoolbesturen en van ouders bij deze wetwijziging over experimenten in hun onderwijssector of in hun regio.
Asks what the added value is of a separate experiments act alongside experiment provisions in sector laws.
They ask to what extent it is desirable for a separate experiments act to exist alongside the experiment provisions in sector laws.
Zij vragen in hoeverre het wenselijk is naast de experimenteerbepalingen in sectorwetten een afzonderlijke experimentenwet te laten bestaan.

33125.s: The bill amends the Dutch road tunnel safety act to set a quantitative risk standard for tunnel safety and to introduce standardised equipment that tunnel managers must use, deviating only under conditions. It also clarifies the tunnel approval process, the role of the safety officer and municipal authorities, and transitional deadlines for existing tunnels.
33125.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation to ministerial regulation by the technical nature of the standards and the need to keep pace with evolving technology, while the Veiligheidsberaad and other ministers are involved in adoption.
q: Deviating from the standardised equipment is possible only in three categories of cases.
Afwijken van de gestandaardiseerde uitrusting kan alleen in drie categorieën van gevallen.
d: adoption of standardised equipment in agreement with other ministers and after advice from Veiligheidsberaad
form and content of tunnel safety plan
p: Tunnel manager may depart from standardised equipment if safety officer is consulted and the same safety level is ensured or EU derogation applies.
The Commissie voor de tunnelveiligheid advice requirement for municipal permits is removed, replaced by submission of risk analysis results, reducing an independent advisory check.

parties: Asks why the Dutch norm exceeds EU requirements, what the costs are, and whether the new tunnel safety officer will avoid the failings of the former commission.
The VVD members wonder why a norm was chosen when the EU directive does not require one.
De leden vragen zich af waarom gekozen is voor een norm terwijl dat volgens de EU-richtlijn niet verplicht is.
Welcomes the clearer national norm and the division of tasks between central and lower governments, finding local involvement acceptable.
The PvdA members are sufficiently convinced of the quality of the safety norm and satisfied with the division of tasks between central and lower government.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie zijn voldoende overtuigd van de kwaliteit van de gestelde norm voor veiligheid en tevreden over de beschreven taakverdeling tussen rijksoverheid en lagere overheden.

Argues that mayors who bear safety responsibility but not costs will keep pushing for extra measures, and wants responsibility for tunnel safety and openings transferred to central government; questions the need for the safety officer.
This gives mayors room to make a fresh plea for extra safety measures each time, all the more so since they bear no responsibility for the costs but do for the safety.

Dit biedt namelijk burgemeesters de ruimte om iedere keer weer een pleidooi af te steken voor extra veiligheidsvoorzieningen, te meer zij geen verantwoording dragen voor de kosten maar wel voor de veiligheid.
Asks how the norm was set, what the costs of standardisation are, and why opening permits are issued by municipalities rather than central government.
The CDA members want to know what extra costs the standardisation of road tunnels entails.
De leden van de CDA-fractie willen weten welke extra kosten de standaardisatie van wegtunnels tot gevolg heeft.
Critical of abolishing the Commissie voor de tunnelveiligheid and asks that its expertise be preserved for national and local governments; asks how the norm compares with other countries.
The SP members are critical of abolishing the Commissie voor de tunnelveiligheid.
De leden van de SP-fractie zijn kritisch over het opheffen van de Commissie voor de tunnelveiligheid.

Worries that the safety officer and fire services have only advisory roles, so tunnel operators alone hold real authority and checks and balances may erode; wants scenario analysis kept as part of the assessment and independence guaranteed.
These members find this very non-binding, because it means only the tunnel operator has real authority.
Deze leden vinden dit erg vrijblijvend, want het betekent dat alleen de tunnelbeheerder echte zeggenschap heeft.

Sees no need to abolish the Commissie voor de tunnelveiligheid, fears splitting knowledge from advice, questions the independence of the safety officer, and asks whether standardised equipment fits local situations and whether municipalities can meet the norm with other instruments.
These members, however, see no need to also abolish the Commissie voor de tunnelveiligheid.
Genoemde leden zien echter niet de noodzaak om daarnaast ook de Commissie voor de tunnelveiligheid op te heffen.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports the tunnel safety bill but objects to the safety norm (applying only to new tunnels, missing a personal-risk norm) and to the consultation requirement for choosing standardised equipment, and advises revision. The government's nader rapport largely accepts these points: it adds a personal-risk element as recommended, extends the norm to existing tunnels with a transition period, adds explanation on consultation and implementation, and adopts the editorial remarks.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for explanation of why no personal-risk norm was included, which the government addressed by stating a group-risk norm was chosen on research advice, with the explanatory memorandum supplemented.
The safety norm in Article 6 was inconsistent in applying only to new tunnels; the government made it generally applicable with a transition period.

Concern that the choice of standardised equipment lacked clarity on the role of the competent municipal authority and the consistency with the discretion to deviate; the government supplemented the explanation but did not change the consultation mechanism.
The Afdeling asked to implement Article 3(2) and Article 14 of Directive 2004/54/EC; the government held these were already implemented and explained how.
Editorial remarks on wording, ordering of Article 6b, and cross-references were adopted.

33161.s: The bill renames and restructures the Dutch work and benefits laws into a single Work according to Capacity Act (Wet werken naar vermogen), moving people who can partly work from the Wajong, Wsw and WWB regimes to municipalities. It introduces wage-dispensation (loondispensatie) with a municipal eligibility assessment, narrows Wajong access to people without work capacity, and sets out transitional rules and municipal ordinance duties.
33161.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations by saying the detailed rules on eligibility, wage value and transition are technical and must be fitted to the pilot experience and the RWI research, and that a monitoring-based order in council is needed to contain excessive benefit use.
q: In a general administrative order, further rules will be set for determining wage value.
In een algemene maatregel van bestuur zullen nadere regels worden gesteld voor het bepalen van de loonwaarde.
d: rules implementing wage-dispensation eligibility and wage-value determination
periods for re-assessment of wage-dispensation eligibility and wage value
transitional rules on wage-dispensation decisions under the pilot
scientific insights supporting assessment of work possibilities
rules on assessing work possibilities for young disabled persons
structural functional limitations and implementation of sick-pay entitlement
municipal reimbursement of benefit costs to UWV
allocation rules for participation budget among municipalities
municipal ordinances on benefit reduction, supplements and special assistance
municipal ordinance on use of re-integration funds
p: Municipalities may reduce wage entitlements of benefit recipients to wage value and set eligibility through an independent third party's advice, with objections limited to procedural review.
Allows an order in council to shift benefit-cost liability onto municipalities, subject to a voorhang procedure and a condition of excessive use.
Delegates the definition of young disabled persons' work capacity assessment to general administrative orders and ministerial regulation with limited consultation.

parties: Supports the bill's principles of focusing on capabilities and asks clarifying questions about labour market assumptions and integration with other decentralisations.
The present bill offers people with a work disability more chance to take up work with a regular employer and participate fully in society.
Het onderhavige wetsvoorstel biedt de mensen met een arbeidshandicap meer kans om bij een reguliere werkgever aan de slag te gaan en volwaardig mee te doen in de maatschappij.
Asks what guarantees citizens have if municipalities implement the law poorly or supervision falls short, and whether municipalities may refuse applications when funds run out.
The PvdA members ask what guarantees there are for citizens if municipalities do not implement the law properly and municipal supervision falls short.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie vragen welke waarborgen er zijn voor de burgers als de gemeenten de wet niet naar behoren uitvoeren en het gemeentelijk toezicht tekort schiet.
Supports the principles and the strengthened municipal role, while raising some questions on implementation.
The responsibility that municipalities receive under this law strengthens their steering role in citizen participation.
De verantwoordelijkheid die de gemeenten door deze wet krijgen versterkt hun regierol in de participatie van burgers.
Supports the aim but insists decentralisation must come with real powers and warns against restrictive rules from above; questions feasibility and the effect on the target group.
Restrictive regulation from above must be prevented.
Knellende regelgeving van bovenaf moet worden voorkomen.
Strongly opposes the bill as harmful and asks the government to justify its labour market assumptions with evidence and to respond to critics.
Can the government substantiate this assumption with facts?
Kan de regering deze aanname onderbouwen met feiten?
Asks questions on welfare inflow, Wajong shifting, and the consequences for AWBZ and Wmo demand, without taking a position.
The D66 members have received the bill and have various questions arising from it.
De leden van de D66-fractie hebben het wetsvoorstel ontvangen en hebben naar aanleiding hiervan verschillende vragen.
Argues the financial framework leaves municipalities too little room for tailored support and asks how the government will monitor effects and adjust policy if the law fails.

The GroenLinks members therefore ask how the government will monitor the effects and effectiveness of this law and whether it intends to adjust policy if the core aim of sustainably guiding people to work cannot be realised in practice.

De leden van de GroenLinks-fractie vragen dan ook op welke wijze de regering de werking van deze wet gaat monitoren (zowel de gevolgen als de effectiviteit) en of de regering voornemens is haar beleid bij te sturen als blijkt dat de kern van de wet, namelijk het duurzaam naar werk begeleiden van mensen, in de praktijk niet waar gemaakt kan worden.
Shares the aim of raising participation of people with disabilities and asks detailed questions on regimes, expertise and compensation principles.
These members share the government's aim of increasing labour participation of people with disabilities, but have some questions about the present bill.
Deze leden delen de doelstelling van de regering om de arbeidsparticipatie van mensen met een beperking te vergroten, maar hebben bij het voorliggende wetsvoorstel nog enkele vragen.
Endorses the aim of simplifying social provisions and avoiding wrong incentives, while questioning whether the structure achieves this.
They ask whether the structure of the bill creates optimal conditions for this.
Zij hebben vragen of de structuur van het wetsvoor stel hiervoor optimale voorwaarden schept.
Asks for clarification on which matters municipalities must regulate by ordinance and how the quota law and job guarantees will work, while backing municipal autonomy.
They still have some questions for clarification about this fourth amendment note.
Zij hebben over deze vierde nota van wijziging nog wel enkele vragen ter verduidelijking.
Welcomes improvements but demands guarantees that promised jobs materialise, asks how the quota and loonwaarde measurement will be legally anchored and checked.
The government must do everything to ensure the promised extra jobs really materialise.
De regering moet alles op alles te zetten om te zorgen dat de beloofde extra banen er ook echt komen.
Strongly opposes the law, arguing it harms people with disabilities, closes sheltered workplaces and cuts benefits, and asks for testing against the UN disability convention and a postponed start.
The SP members have serious concerns about the position of people with a work disability, the unemployed and people on low incomes.
De leden van de SP-fractie maken zich grote zorgen om de positie van mensen met een arbeidsbeperking, werklozen en mensen met een laag inkomen.
Supports the aim of the law but raises critical questions on job guarantees, eligibility and whether regions get real room for tailored arrangements without central instructions.
Although the CDA members agree with the main lines of the law, they still have a number of critical questions about the amendment note.
Hoewel de leden van de CDA-fractie het dus eens zijn met de hoofdlijnen van de wet, hebben zij nog wel een aantal kritische vragen bij de nota van wijziging.

Worries whether the law will achieve regular employment, the transition of reassessed Wajongers to assistance, and the scope of delegated powers that could limit municipal discretion, asking for parliamentary pre-consultation.
However, the D66 members see that through some delegation provisions the room for tailored policy could be considerably restricted.
Wel zien de leden van de D66-fractie dat middels enkele delegatiebepalingen de ruimte voor maatwerk flink kan worden ingeperkt.
Asks detailed questions on quota contours, sheltered work, regional workbedrijven and whether municipalities can use existing exemptions for SW-bedrijven.
These members would like to put the following questions to the government for answer.
Genoemde leden willen graag de onderstaande vragen ter beantwoording aan de regering stellen.
Fears serious consequences for income security and feasibility, shares the Council of State's doubts about municipal capacity, and asks that the right to tailored support be legally anchored.
The GroenLinks members also share the Council of State's doubt about whether municipalities are sufficiently enabled to carry out the tasks assigned to them.
De leden van de GroenLinks-fractie onderschrijven ook de twijfel van de Raad van State of gemeenten wel voldoende in staat worden gesteld om de toebedeelde taken uit te voeren.
Questions whether incentives and structures sufficiently promote transition to regular work and whether protective employment rules should be relaxed for workers with disabilities.
They ask both whether the proposals contain sufficient incentives to move on to regular work and whether the proposed structures sufficiently promote job opportunities.
Zij vragen zich zowel af of de voorstellen voldoende prikkels bevatten om door te stromen naar regulier werk als wel of de voorgestelde structuren de kansen op werk voldoende bevorderen.
Asks how appeals work for municipal pre-selection and whether the AMvB on sheltered work will go through a pre-consultation procedure with parliament.
Can people file objections and appeals against the municipality's pre-selection for sheltered work assessment?
Kunnen mensen bezwaar en beroep aantekenen voor de voorselectie voor de indicering van beschut werk van de gemeente?
Welcomes the amendment allowing municipalities to take over benefit recipients from UWV and asks the government to respond to FNV criticism of unfulfilled agreements.
They consider it an improvement that this proposal makes it possible for people in the wage-cost subsidy target group receiving a UWV benefit to fall under municipal responsibility.

Zij vinden het een verbetering dat met dit voorstel het mogelijk wordt gemaakt dat ook personen die tot de doelgroep loonkostensubsidie behoren en een uitkering van het UWV ontvangen tot de verantwoordelijkheid van gemeenten gaan behoren.
Questions whether government agreements with social partners not reflected in the bill are being sent to parliament and whether promised commitments are being kept.
Can the government confirm that the FNV agreed to the commitment that the existing Wajong population will be re-assessed?
Kan de regering bevestigen dat de FNV heeft ingestemd met de afspraak «Het zittend bestand Wajong wordt herkeurd;
Asks for more detail on national criteria to be set by AMvB for UWV assessments, timing, and financing of the assessment, and on FNV concerns about inconsistent wording.
Can the government elaborate on these remarks, ask these members.
Kan de regering nader ingaan op deze opmerkingen, zo vragen deze leden.

Finds the amendment vague, questions why UWV's advisory role is combined with municipal procedural review and whether municipalities can make independent pre-selections, creating two diverging eligibility groups.
The SGP members cannot shake the impression that the amendment note is highly vague.
De leden van de SGP-fractie kunnen zich niet aan de indruk ontworstelen dat de nota van wijziging in hoge mate aan wazigheid onderhevig is.
Warns that local discretion and budget constraints in municipal pre-selection expose people to arbitrariness, and objects that substantive UWV assessments cannot be appealed.
As a result, people in the target group are left exposed to local arbitrariness.
Hierdoor worden mensen die tot de doelgroep behoren overgeleverd aan lokale willekeur.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advises on the fourth amendment note to the Participatiewet implementing bill, doubting that the instruments introduced (wage cost subsidy, sheltered work, Wsw closure) will suffice for municipalities to reach the target groups, and asks for reconsideration. The government's reply rejects reconsidering the amendment, clarifies the explanatory memorandum, and commits to talks with VNG and a monitoring 'thermometer' while keeping its chosen instruments.
concerns: The Afdeling doubts that the labour market and job commitments will absorb the growing municipal target group, and the government rejects reconsidering the amendment.
The Afdeling questions why the more expensive wage cost subsidy would be more effective than wage dispensation; the government defends the choice and clarifies the explanatory memorandum.
The Afdeling questions how municipalities can control Wsw costs and the pension problem after closing intake; the government points to a monitoring thermometer and VNG talks.
The Afdeling questions requiring an employment relationship for sheltered work and the high costs that follow; the government maintains the choice.
The Afdeling warns that mandatory inter-municipal cooperation undermines municipal regulatory roles; the government says cooperation is a last-resort delegation power.
The Afdeling raised redactional points, which the government has incorporated into the amendment note.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports integrating benefit schemes, pooling reintegration budgets and introducing wage-cost subsidy (loondispensatie) under the Wwnv, but raises major concerns about the evidence base for employer willingness, the Wsw's financial sustainability, the overlap between target groups, and the long transitional regimes that protect existing rights. The government reply largely accepts these points, adding analysis, clarifications and some technical amendments, while maintaining the policy choices and the transitional arrangements.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for a fuller analysis of how loondispensatie affects demand for low-skilled labour and of employer willingness; the government added supporting examples and labour-market reasoning but kept its position.
The Afdeling found the boundary between the loondispensatie target group and the Wsw target group unclear and asked for clarification, which the government provided in the memorie van toelichting.

The Afdeling argued that the long transitional regimes (eerbiedigende werking) lacked substantive justification under Article 1 of the First Protocol ECHR and advised a shorter transition; the government justified the choice but did not shorten it.

The Afdeling raised serious concerns about municipal capacity and the financial viability of Wsw companies under the new regime and asked for analysis of cumulative municipal risks; the government pointed to a restructuring facility and transition support without fully resolving the concern.
The Afdeling asked to specify or clarify the delegation in Wsw article 12(4); the government removed the delegation and placed the rules directly in the statute.
The Afdeling asked for clearer Wajong structure and a corrected definition of re-integratievoorziening; the government explained and adjusted the definition and text.

33215.s: This bill amends the 2012 departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Finance (IXB) to incorporate a one-off supplementary budget for the European Stabilisation Mechanism (ESM), with amounts in thousands of euros and retroactive effect to 30 May if published late. It contains no delegation of rule-making power to the executive; its effect is a budgetary appropriation approved by statute.
q: Whereas the need has arisen to amend the departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Finance (IXB) for 2012, in connection with the establishment of the European Stabilisation Mechanism (ESM);

Alzo Wij in overweging genomen hebben, dat de noodzaak is gebleken van een wijziging van de departementale begrotingsstaat van het Ministerie van Financiën (IXB) voor het jaar 2012, samenhangend met de instelling van het Europees Stabiliteitsmechanisme (ESM);

33224.s: The bill amends the Dutch member-of-parliament allowance laws for both chambers to adjust travel allowances after the Fiscal Simplification Act 2010 and to provide a service car for the Speakers of the House and Senate. It also sets out how the allowances are taxed and provides for annual indexation of certain amounts by ministerial regulation.
33224.j: The memorandum states that use of the service car has no additional costs, which is offered as the basis for the arrangement; the indexation delegations are presented as technical adjustments.
q: The use of the service car therefore does not result in additional costs.
Het gebruik van de dienstauto heeft om deze reden geen meerkosten tot gevolg.
d: I.A.3 (Art. 7 Wet schadeloosstelling leden Tweede Kamer)
II.A (Art. 13 Wet vergoedingen leden Eerste Kamer, cost formula subsection 3)
annual indexation of service car price per kilometre
II.C (Art. 17 Wet vergoedingen leden Eerste Kamer, subsection 2)
adjustment of travel allowance to civil servant travel rates
I.E (Art. 12a Wet schadeloosstelling leden Tweede Kamer, subsection 5)
safety or individual workplace analysis deviations from service car rules
p: Provides the Speakers with a service car at a capped per-kilometre price, with detailed cost formula and limited deviation grounds for safety or workplace analysis.

parties: The CDA asks whether a party-funding arrangement that routes member income into the party treasury and then reimburses declared costs fits the bill and may contradict its intent.

However, these members ask how the proposed amendment to the fiscal work-cost scheme relates to the arrangement at one fractie, whose members deposit their income into the party treasury and then declare costs to the party.

Wel vragen deze leden, hoe de voorgestelde aanpassing aan de fiscale werkkostenregeling zich verhoudt tot de regeling bij één fractie, waarvan de leden hun inkomen storten in de partijkas, waarna diezelfde leden kosten declareren bij de partij.

33350.s: The bill approves the Besluit aanpassing wetten inzake verhoging AOW-leeftijd, an general administrative order (AMvB) that amends statutes to adjust them to the raised AOW (state pension) age. It also repeals the temporary delegation basis in article V of the Wet verhoging AOW- en pensioenrichtleeftijd once the approved order enters into force.
33350.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation as necessary to adjust laws to the raised AOW age and prevent unacceptable consequences, with a commitment to repeal the temporary basis once the order takes effect.
q: Under article V, first paragraph, of the Act raising the AOW and pension age, the legislature gave the government the power to amend laws by general administrative order

Op grond van artikel V, eerste lid, van de Wet verhoging AOW- en pensioenrichtleeftijd is door de wetgever aan de regering de bevoegdheid gegeven om bij algemene maatregel van bestuur wetten te wijzigen
d: Artikel V Wet verhoging AOW- en pensioenrichtleeftijd (as referenced)
amending statutes to adjust them to the raised AOW age
p: Artikel V, eerste lid, Wet verhoging AOW- en pensioenrichtleeftijd (as referenced)

The government may amend statutes by general administrative order where necessary for application or to prevent unacceptable consequences, bypassing ordinary legislation, though the order must later be approved by statute and the delegation expires.

parties: Asks how far the scope of the bill reaches, whether other laws must change, and whether future amendments can be made by general administrative order after the delegation basis lapses.
The VVD members assume that through this law the delegation basis in the Wet verhoging AOW- en pensioenrichtleeftijd lapses.
De leden van de VVD-fractie gaan ervan uit dat door deze wet de delegatiegrondslag in de Wet verhoging AOW- en pensioenrichtleeftijd vervalt.
Objects to the speed and scale of the reform, questions whether the government understands its consequences, and warns about citizens' trust and loans for those affected.
Moreover, the PVV members consider it irresponsible to carry out such far-reaching statutory changes in this way and at this speed.
Bovendien achten de leden van de PVV-fractie het onverantwoord om op deze wijze en met deze snelheid dit soort vergaande wetswijzigingen door te voeren.
Asks for examples of when the bill permits amending laws where necessary or to prevent unacceptable effects, and for the consequences of the coalition side agreement.
The CDA members note that the bill grants permission to amend laws insofar as this is necessary for their application or to prevent unacceptable consequences.

De leden van de CDA-fractie constateren dat er met het onderhavige wetsvoorstel toestemming wordt gegeven om wetten te wijzigen voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor de toepassing van die wetten of ter voorkoming van onaanvaardbare gevolgen.
Approves the amendments but asks how the faster AOW increase agreed in the side agreement relates to the delegation provision withdrawn by article II, and about transitional arrangements.
These members are further curious how the reached side agreement relates to article II of the present bill, in which the delegation provision is withdrawn.
Deze leden zijn voorts benieuwd hoe het bereikte deelakkoord zich verhoudt tot artikel II van het onderhavige wetsvoorstel waarin de delegatiebepaling wordt ingetrokken.
Accepts the alignment of other statutes with the staged age increase and asks why not all laws were adjusted and when remaining laws and pension schemes will be updated.
These members can agree with the adjustment of the various other laws to the previously decided staged increase of the AOW age.
Deze leden kunnen zich vinden in de aanpassing van de diverse andere wetten aan de eerder besloten stapsgewijze verhoging van de AOW-leeftijd.

33404.s: The bill ends the tax-free treatment of commuting (woon-werkverkeer) for employers and employees and redefines commuting for income and wage tax, with transitional rules for public transport cards and company cars. It aims to save about 1.5 billion euro structurally and sets out transitional provisions effective from 1 January 2013.
33404.j: The memorandum justifies the ministerial regulation for valuing commuting transport by noting that the economic value of such transport is difficult to determine, so the detailed valuation rules are left to a ministerial regulation.
q: Because it is very difficult to determine the economic value of employer-organised commuting transport, the new article 13(3)(b) of the Wage Tax Act 1964 provides for detailed rules to be set by ministerial regulation.

Omdat het erg lastig is om de economische waarde van het genot van vervoer vanwege de inhoudingsplichtige aangaande het woon-werkverkeer vast te stellen, wordt in het nieuwe artikel 13, derde lid, onderdeel b, van de Wet LB 1964 de mogelijkheid geboden om bij ministeriële regeling nadere regels te stellen
d: Artikel II, onderdeel B (artikel 13, derde lid, onderdeel b, Wet LB 1964)
valuation of employer-organised transport for commuting

parties: Asks whether the 600 million business-travel allowance moves into the werkkostenregeling and what that means for employers and the administrative burden.
Does placing it in the free space not mean employers and employees must keep distinguishing between commuting kilometres and business kilometres?
Betekent het onderbrengen in de vrije ruimte niet dat werkgevers en werknemers een onderscheid moeten blijven maken tussen kilometers voor woon-werkverkeer en zakelijke kilometers?
Opposes the commuting tax and the replacement by a higher insurance tax; states the draagkrachtbeginsel was overshadowed by greening.
The ability-to-pay principle was completely overshadowed by greening.
Het draagkrachtbeginsel werd geheel overvleugeld door de vergroening.
Asks which occupations count as ambulant, whether they face higher burdens, and whether a graduated company-car addition per private kilometre was examined.
Will the government ensure that practitioners of occupations described as ambulant are not saddled with higher burdens?
Gaat de regering er zorg voor dragen dat beoefenaars van beroepen die als ambulant worden omschreven, niet worden opgezadeld met hogere lasten?
Asks the consequences of the Harbers/Plasterk amendment for the bill and whether the government will withdraw it.
To what extent is the government considering withdrawing this bill?
In hoeverre overweegt de regering om dit wetsvoorstel in te trekken?

Questions administrative burden, the broad definition for ambulant workers, the one-year detachment rule that could be circumvented, and disappointment that compensation for allowances is not possible.
Regrets that the bill will likely not proceed, citing expected air quality and traffic benefits, and asks for internal notes and koopkracht effects.
The GroenLinks members are disappointed that this bill will most likely not proceed.
De leden van de GroenLinks-fractie zijn teleurgesteld dat voorliggend wetsvoorstel naar alle waarschijnlijk geen doorgang zal vinden.

v.summary: The Council of State advisory division advised on the bill reforming the tax treatment of commuting (woon-werkverkeer), raising concerns about the rationale and abrupt timing of the measure, the distinction between commuting and business travel, the company car rules and the valuation of public transport passes. The government's reply largely accepts the timing and reasoning points, defends its chosen definition, and adds clarifications on employer-organised transport while keeping the core measure.
concerns: The Council questioned why the commuting regime was chosen as cover for the transfer tax cut and urged a more gradual introduction; the government adjusted the explanatory memorandum but kept the 2013 timing to meet the budget target.

The Council found the new commuting definition, borrowed from VAT, unconvincing and asked for justification; the government defended a hybrid definition and argued the new regularity test reduces disputes.

The Council noted that the company car 500-km threshold and forfait were not adjusted for commuting kilometres; the government stated the coalition agreement limits the change to counting commuting kilometres as private.

The Council asked the explanatory memorandum to be supplemented on valuation of public transport passes and employer-organised transport; the government added the employer-transport passage and found the rest sufficient.
The Council gave editorial corrections to article cross-references, which the government adopted.

33422.s: The bill implements EU framework decision 2009/829/JBZ by adding a new Book 5 to the Dutch Code of Criminal Procedure, allowing supervision measures imposed abroad as alternatives to pre-trial detention to be recognised and enforced in the Netherlands, and vice versa. It sets out the Public Prosecution Service's competence to decide on recognition, grounds for refusal, and the transfer of supervision to probation services.
33422.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation of additional supervision measures by reciprocity and flexibility given the diversity of national criminal law, and the central role of the Public Prosecution Service by efficiency and the need for uniform handling.
q: By general administrative order, supervision measures referred to in the first paragraph, under g, may be designated, insofar as the Netherlands is the executing Member State.
Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen toezichtmaatregelen als bedoeld in het eerste lid, onder g, worden aangewezen, voor zover het Nederland als uitvoerende lidstaat betreft.
d: designating additional supervision measures recognisable in the Netherlands
p: The Public Prosecution Service is given competence to decide on recognition of foreign supervision decisions and to transmit Dutch decisions abroad, with a duty to consult foreign authorities.
The Public Prosecution Service decides on refusal grounds, and most mandatory grounds are limited and enumerated, with the right to seek court review through kort geding."

parties: Worries that the measures could undermine the criminal procedure against the suspect and asks how the flight-risk criterion and the legality of foreign supervision measures will be assessed.
In their view there is a real danger that the proposed measures will harm the criminal proceedings against the suspect or lead to abandoning the values of the Dutch criminal justice system.

Wat hen betreft bestaat er een reëel gevaar dat de voorgestelde maatregelen ten koste gaan van de tegen de verdachte lopende strafprocedure of leiden tot het loslaten van de aan het Nederlandse strafrechtstelsel verbonden waarden.
Argues the framework takes too formalistic a view of the executing state's role and questions limited dual criminality review, which may matter if breaches lead to surrender.
The PvdA members are of the view that the bill takes too formalistic a view of the position of the executing Member State.
De leden van de PvdA-fractie zijn van mening dat het wetsvoorstel uitgaat van een te formalistische kijk op de positie van de uitvoerende lidstaat.
Rejects deeper EU criminal cooperation and asks why non-resident suspects would be treated differently, and about enforcement and cost of supervision violations.
These members note that they reject ever further criminal cooperation between EU Member States.
Deze leden merken op dat zij een steeds verdergaande strafrechtelijke samenwerking tussen lidstaten van de EU afwijzen.

Asks why supervision measures are set by AMvB rather than in statute, questions the quality of supervision abroad, and raises concern about the lack of legal protection against decisions on supervision.
Supports European criminal cooperation but asks whether other states have comparable supervision arrangements and about legal protection standards and information exchange.

They endorse that European cooperation in criminal law serves the interests of the Netherlands and its citizens, and that a corresponding level of legal protection in the EU contributes to the trust needed for criminal cooperation.

Zij onderschrijven dat Europese samenwerking op het terrein van strafrecht in het belang is van Nederland en zijn burgers en dat een corresponderend niveau van rechtsbescherming in de EU bijdraagt aan het voor de strafrechtelijke samenwerking benodigde vertrouwen.
Welcomes the bill for taking account of suspects' position, but asks for annual reporting and how non-resident suspects' risks are mitigated.
They consider it a good development that further steps are taken in criminal cooperation between Member States and that the position of suspects in the Member States is also taken into account.

Zij vinden het een goede ontwikkeling dat verdere stappen worden gezet in de strafrechtelijke samenwerking tussen lidstaten en dat daarbij ook de positie van verdachten in de lidstaten wordt meegenomen.

v.summary: The Raad van State's advisory division supports the bill implementing Framework Decision 2009/829/JHA on mutual recognition of supervision measures as an alternative to pre-trial detention, but objects that the bill omits the 20-working-day extension of the recognition deadline when an appeal is lodged against the issuing decision, and advises amending article 8 accordingly. In the government's reply, the minister disagrees on the interpretation of 'decision' in article 12(2), defends the existing wording, and largely declines the editorial suggestions, though some were adopted.
concerns: The Afdeling argues article 12(2) of the framework decision requires a 20-working-day extension of the recognition deadline when an appeal is lodged, and that article 8 should be supplemented; the minister disagrees on the interpretation and does not amend the bill.

Several editorial suggestions are partly adopted, including redrafting article 3(2) and referring to article 3:10(3) of the Wet wederzijdse erkenning, while the proposal to inform the person of the recognition decision is rejected and the article 80 Sv reference is deferred to a separate bill.

33503.s: The bill amends the Waterwet, the Invoeringswet Waterwet, the Waterschapswet, the Wet op de economische delicten and the Algemene wet bestuursrecht to improve the workability and enforceability of the Waterwet, simplify the pollution levy and abolish the Commission of advice on water legislation. Key changes include clarifying mandate and indeplaatsstelling powers, removing provincial approval of water board management plans, narrowing appeal routes and allowing water boards' executive committees to adopt projectplannen.
33503.j: The memorandum justifies changes as improving workability and enforceability, reducing specific supervision in line with the Bestuursakkoord Water, and clarifying legal uncertainty.
q: The government chooses to reduce specific supervision.
De regering kiest voor het terugdringen van specifiek toezicht.
d: designating non-state bodies to manage parts of national waters
designation of competent authority, exercisable by mandate
p: I, H and I (art. 3.12 and 3.13 Waterwet)
Ministerial instruction and substitution powers toward water boards and provinces are broadened to cover results not achieved in time or properly, not only decisions.
Provincial approval of water board management plans is abolished, reducing specific supervisory control over water boards.
Appeal against project plan approval is limited to parties who submitted objections, and appeal against management plans is excluded.
Provincial executive may also exercise powers of entry and access to land and works for water management.
Several Waterwet decisions, including management plan vaststelling and preparatory decisions, are excluded from judicial appeal.
Executive committees of water boards may adopt project plans, with retroactive effect to 22 December 2009.

parties: Asks where the line lies between a limited and a high tariff increase and whether other companies will pay more, and how negative water-quality effects will be prevented.
The VVD members can agree with simplifying the pollution levy, but ask where the line lies between a 'limited' tariff increase and a 'high' tariff increase.

De leden van de VVD-fractie kunnen zich goed vinden in een vereenvoudiging van de verontreinigingsheffing, maar vragen waar de grens ligt tussen een «beperkte» tariefstijging en een «hoge» tariefstijging.
Worries that the simplification abandons the polluter-pays principle required by the Water Framework Directive and asks for quantitative justification.
The PvdA members express concern that the new simplified levy scheme abandons the principle that 'the largest polluters pay the most'.

De leden van de PvdA-fractie spreken de zorg uit over het feit dat met de nieuwe vereenvoudigde regeling rondom de verontreinigingsheffing het principe «de grootste vervuilers betalen het meest» wordt losgelaten.
Has no questions on the bill.
The PVV members have noted the amendment and have no need at present to ask questions.

De leden van de PVV-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van de Wijziging van de Waterwet en enkele andere wetten (aanvulling en verbetering; vereenvoudiging van de verontreinigingsheffing; opheffing van de Commissie van advies inzake de waterstaatswetgeving) en hebben thans geen behoefte aan het stellen van vragen.

Questions the unexplained reversal of the Madlener motion and the lack of justification for scrapping the heavy-metal levy and the CAW, and asks that the CAW be kept until the new Omgevingswet is in force.
The SP members note that the Explanatory Memorandum insufficiently explains the considerations behind the proposal to abolish the CAW.
De leden van de SP-fractie constateren dat de Memorie van Toelichting onvoldoende aangeeft welke overwegingen hebben geleid tot het voorstel voor de opheffing van de CAW.
Asks how the polluter-pays principle is still met, how the knowledge of the CAW will be transferred to the RLI, and what control costs are.
These members note that by abolishing the levy on discharges of heavy metals and salts, source control is abandoned and they would welcome a response.
Deze leden constateren dat door het afschaffen van de heffing voor het lozen van zware metalen en zouten bestrijding aan de bron wordt losgelaten en ontvangen hierop graag een reactie.
Asks for justification of the tariff increase and cross-subsidy, the savings from abolishing the CAW, and whether the RLI has adequate resources.
The D66 members ask the government to explain what savings abolishing the CAW produces.
De leden van de D66-fractie vragen de regering toe te lichten welke besparing het opheffen van de CAW oplevert.
Asks how the CAW's long-term expertise will be safeguarded and why the CAW is not kept until the Omgevingswet is in force, and notes water boards' support for reconsidering abolition.
These members ask how the CAW's knowledge, which has existed for more than 100 years, will be safeguarded in the long term, for example within advisory councils that are not abolished.
Genoemde leden vragen hoe deze kennis van de CAW, die al meer dan 100 jaar bestaat, voor de lange termijn wordt geborgd, bijvoorbeeld binnen adviesraden die niet worden opgeheven.
Has no questions on the bill.
The GroenLinks members have noted the amendment and have no need at present to ask questions.

De leden van de GroenLinks-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van de Wijziging van de Waterwet en enkele andere wetten (aanvulling en verbetering; vereenvoudiging van de verontreinigingsheffing; opheffing van de Commissie van advies inzake de waterstaatswetgeving) en hebben thans geen behoefte aan het stellen van vragen.
Opposes abolishing the CAW, arguing its independent advice remains important for water-safety law and upcoming decisions, and that the Explanatory Memorandum gives no sound justification.
These members find that the advice of the independent and experienced committee will remain of undiminished great importance in the coming years.
Deze leden vinden dat in de komende jaren het advies van de onafhankelijke en ervaren commissie van onverminderd groot belang blijft.
Has no questions on the bill.
The Partij voor de Dieren members have noted the amendment and have no need at present to ask questions.

De leden van de Partij voor de Dieren-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van de Wijziging van de Waterwet en enkele andere wetten (aanvulling en verbetering; vereenvoudiging van de verontreinigingsheffing; opheffing van de Commissie van advies inzake de waterstaatswetgeving) en hebben thans geen behoefte aan het stellen van vragen.
Has no questions on the bill.
The 50PLUS members have noted the amendment and have no need at present to ask questions.

De leden van de 50PLUS-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van de Wijziging van de Waterwet en enkele andere wetten (aanvulling en verbetering; vereenvoudiging van de verontreinigingsheffing; opheffing van de Commissie van advies inzake de waterstaatswetgeving) en hebben thans geen behoefte aan het stellen van vragen.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division issued critical advice on the Waterwet amendment bill, objecting to extending the duty to accept dredged material and soil to owners of non-adjacent land, to dropping 'regulier' without adequate justification, to abolishing the advisory commission on water law, and to simplifying the pollution levy in ways that may conflict with the EU Water Framework Directive. The government's reply (nader rapport) states it postponed the dredging-duty extension to the Omgevingswet, reasoned the abolition and levy changes, and clarified the explanatory memorandum, while not adopting all points.
concerns: Extending the duty to accept dredged material to owners of non-adjacent land interferes with property rights and needs adequate justification; the government postponed this to the Omgevingswet.
Filling the duty of owners of non-adjacent land fully by ministerial regulation or water board bylaw exceeds the appropriate level of regulation; core elements should be in an AMvB.
The explanatory memorandum insufficiently justifies abolishing the Commissie van advies inzake de waterstaatswetgeving, given the cabinet policy and the 2011 letter listing it as surviving.

Simplifying the pollution levy by dropping heavy metals and salts shifts costs to oxygen-binding substance dischargers and must be reconciled with Article 9 of the Water Framework Directive and EU state aid rules; the government argued it is compatible.
The explanatory memorandum does not address whether removing the levy on heavy metals and salts will increase discharges or whether flanking measures are needed; the government judged none necessary.
A redactional remark suggests specifying that the ministerial regulation covers waters managed by the state and the bylaw covers waters managed by the water board.

33512.s: The bill makes unlawful residence of adult foreigners in the Netherlands a punishable offence (overtreding) under a new article 108a of the Vreemdelingenwet 2000, fined up to the second category, with exemption during the departure period and a rule that enforcement of a fine does not block departure or deportation. It also adds repeated unlawful residence as a ground for issuing a severe entry ban under article 66a.
33512.j: The memorandum justifies the criminalisation as needed to make the return policy more effective, presenting it as an addition to the Returns Directive as a last resort after administrative measures fail.
q: The present bill changes that. It thereby increases the effectiveness of criminalising unlawful residence.
Het voorliggende wetsvoorstel brengt daar verandering in. Hiermee wordt de effectiviteit van de strafbaarstelling van illegaal verblijf vergroot.
p: Makes unlawful residence a criminal offence enforced via police and OM penalty orders, expanding state coercive power over foreigners, with the explanatory memorandum noting prosecution discretion and a possible individual assessment by the court.
Artikel I A (art. 66a, zevende lid Vw)
Allows the minister to issue a severe entry ban after repeated criminal unlawful residence, with the memorandum stating it will be applied restrictively and specified by general administrative order.

parties: Asks why the offence is classified as a misdemeanour (overtreding) rather than a crime, why the fine level was chosen, and how the criminal and return policies relate, including overlap between administrative and criminal enforcement powers.

Stresses criminal law as ultimum remedium and questions whether criminal sanctions can come before the administrative return instruments required by the Return Directive and CJEU case law, and whether a fine or substitute detention may obstruct return.
In the view of these members, a criminal response must also be appropriate in terms of the moment at which it is deployed.
Naar de mening van deze leden moet een strafrechtelijke reactie ook passend zijn in de zin van het moment waarop die wordt ingezet.
Asks why the offence is a misdemeanour instead of a crime and how other EU member states have framed illegal residence in criminal law.
These members ask the government which considerations led to treating the offence as an overtreding rather than a misdrijf.
Deze leden vragen de regering welke overwegingen ertoe hebben geleid de genoemde strafbaarstelling als overtreding te beschouwen en niet als een misdrijf.

Argues the criminalisation is unnecessary and counterproductive, questions the evidence of deterrence, and doubts the added value given existing entry bans, and raises concerns about prosecution workload and use of administrative powers as evidence for criminal cases.
It has been insufficiently substantiated why the government believes criminalisation will lead to less illegal residence.
Onvoldoende is onderbouwd waarom de regering van mening is dat strafbaarstelling zal leiden tot minder illegaal verblijf.

Supports tackling illegal residence but questions the added value and effectiveness of a generic criminal offence, asks for evidence on other countries, and cites the Council of State's and ACVZ's doubts about enforcement.
In that light, these members ask the government to respond to the Council of State's serious doubts about the added value of a generic criminal offence.

Voornoemde leden vragen de regering in dat perspectief in te gaan op de ernstige twijfel van de Afdeling advisering van de Raad van State over de meerwaarde die een generieke strafbaarstelling nog heeft.
Holds principled objections to criminalising illegality, disputes the claimed link between illegality and crime, and asks for empirical evidence of effectiveness and proportionality.
The D66 members have principled objections to making illegality a criminal offence.
De leden van de D66-fractie hebben principiële bezwaren tegen het strafbaar stellen van illegaliteit.

Questions necessity and effects, raises children's rights and risks that victims or parents avoid police, medical care or school, and asks how the lex certa principle is satisfied given the Council of State's objection.
The ChristenUnie members have taken note of the bill and have questions about its usefulness and necessity.
De leden van de ChristenUnie-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van het wetsvoorstel en hebben vragen bij nut en noodzaak.

Argues criminal law should not be used for symbolic legislation, that the assumed social burden is unsubstantiated, and warns that criminalisation deters victims of trafficking and exploitation from contacting police, and questions how children's rights are safeguarded.
They fear that this bill must be counted among such symbolic legislation.
Zij vrezen dat dit wetsvoorstel daartoe gerekend moet worden.
Asks which countries criminalise illegality beyond entry-ban violations, requests evidence for the claimed deterrent effect, and raises the possibility that a strict asylum image is undermined.
These members request substantiation for the government's claim that criminalising illegality has a deterrent effect.
Deze leden vragen een onderbouwing van de stelling van de regering dat van strafbaarstelling van illegaliteit een afschrikkende werking uitgaat.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on a bill criminalising unlawful residence of adult foreigners in the Netherlands as a misdemeanour, raising doubts about necessity, lex certa, consistency with the Return Directive and social side-effects, and advised reconsideration. The government's reply rejected the main objection on necessity, adopted the Return Directive points by removing detention as a main penalty and adding a clause that enforcement may not obstruct removal, and explained the other points in the explanatory memorandum.
concerns: The Afdeling doubted the added value of a generic criminal offence of illegal residence beyond the existing offence of violating an entry ban, since those reached first-time offenders would receive an entry ban anyway.

The Afdeling found the offence too broad given many exceptions and defences, contrary to the lex certa principle, and advised precision; the government did not adopt this but clarified that the Public Prosecution Service will issue enforcement guidelines.

The Afdeling advised aligning the bill with the Return Directive as interpreted by the CJEU, including suspending penalty enforcement where removal is possible and applying administrative return measures first; the government removed detention as a main penalty and added a clause that enforcement may not hinder removal, but rejected the requirement that administrative measures precede criminal sanctions.

The Afdeling warned that criminalising illegal residence may deter victims of exploitation and violence from reporting to police and discourage voluntary departure or new applications, and asked for convincing motivation; the government clarified exceptions and reporting protections in the memorandum without accepting that the effects would arise.

33611.s: The bill modernises Dutch arbitration law by amending Book 6 and Book 10 of the Civil Code and the Fourth Book of the Code of Civil Procedure, shifting more procedural matters to party agreement and reducing court involvement in arbitral proceedings. It adds rules on interim measures, joinder, third-party intervention, appeal, and recognition of foreign awards, while leaving the explanatory memorandum unavailable in the text provided.
q: Unless the parties have made a choice of law, the substantive validity of an arbitration agreement is determined by Dutch law, departing from article 154.
Tenzij de partijen een rechtskeuze hebben gemaakt, wordt in afwijking van artikel 154 de materiële geldigheid van een overeenkomst tot arbitrage bepaald door Nederlands recht.
p: Clarifies that public-law bodies cannot invoke their own internal rules to contest capacity to enter arbitration agreements, limiting executive-body escape routes from arbitration commitments.

Shifts several procedural decisions (appointment, removal, challenge of arbitrators, evidence) from courts to arbitral tribunals or party agreement, with the voorzieningenrechter retaining residual competence.

parties: Asks whether consumer arbitration clauses should be blacklisted, whether the Dutch regime stays competitive, and why certain procedural choices (time limits, institutional challenge, enforcement) were made.
Those members note that the time limits for arbitral appeal, annulment and the exequatur petition start when the arbitral award is dispatched.

Voornoemde leden constateren dat de termijnen voor het arbitraal beroep, vernietigingsberoep en het indienen van een verzoekschrift tot het verkrijgen van een exequatur aanvangen op het moment dat het arbitraal vonnis wordt verzonden.
Questions whether access to the state judge is being weakened, whether parties are truly equal when opting out, and whether the review structure (Hof versus rechtbank) is efficient.
These members note that the bill gives parties more scope than current law to agree otherwise than prescribed.
Deze leden merken op dat het wetsvoorstel partijen meer dan het huidige recht de mogelijkheid biedt om anders dan is voorgeschreven overeen te komen.
Worries about transparency, control, consumer costs and privacy in arbitration, and about the narrowing of access to annulment review and unclear challenge grounds.
These members attach importance to possibilities of control and transparency.
Deze leden hechten belang aan controlemogelijkheden en transparantie.
Welcomes the modernisation and the broad consultation, noting the Raad van State advice was supportive.
They welcome the amendments that modernise arbitration law and remove obstacles to its use.
Zij verwelkomen de wijzigingsvoorstellen die leiden tot modernisering van het arbitragerecht en tot opheffing van belemmeringen voor het gebruik van arbitrage.

33800.s: The bill removes protection for writings lacking original character and personal stamp of the author, by deleting the word 'alle' in article 10 and removing the press-related categories in article 15 of the Auteurswet. It also renumbers article 15 paragraphs and sets entry into force by royal decree.
33800.j: The memorandum excerpt does not justify any delegation or new power; it only notes that writings lacking originality receive only the protection available under the writings-protection regime, decided case by case.
